docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.csrf-cookie.domain
docs.description: Cookie domain. Specifies the domain within which this cookie should be presented. The form of the domain name is specified by RFC 2965. A domain name begins with a dot (.foo.com) and means that the cookie is visible to servers in a specified Domain Name System (DNS) zone (for example, www.foo.com, but not a.b.foo.com). By default, cookies are only returned to the server that sent them.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.csrf-cookie.http-only
docs.description: true if this cookie contains the HttpOnly attribute. This means that the cookie should not be accessible to scripting engines, like javascript.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.csrf-cookie.max-age
docs.description: The maximum age of the cookie, specified in seconds. By default, {@code -1} indicating the cookie will persist until browser shutdown. A positive value indicates that the cookie will expire after that many seconds have passed. Note that the value is the maximum age when the cookie will expire, not the cookie's current age. A negative value means that the cookie is not stored persistently and will be deleted when the Web browser exits. A zero value causes the cookie to be deleted.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.csrf-cookie.name
docs.description: Cookie name. Constructs a cookie with a specified name and value. The name must conform to RFC 2965. That means it can contain only ASCII alphanumeric characters and cannot contain commas, semicolons, or white space or begin with a {@code $} character. The cookie's name cannot be changed after creation. By default, cookies are created according to the RFC 2965 cookie specification. Cookie names are automatically calculated assigned by CAS at runtime, and there is usually no need to customize the name or assign it a different value unless a special use case warrants the change.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.csrf-cookie.path
docs.description: Cookie path. Specifies a path for the cookie to which the client should return the cookie. The cookie is visible to all the pages in the directory you specify, and all the pages in that directory's subdirectories. A cookie's path must include the servlet that set the cookie, for example, /catalog, which makes the cookie visible to all directories on the server under /catalog. Consult RFC 2965 (available on the Internet) for more information on setting path names for cookies.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.csrf-cookie.same-site-policy
docs.description:
If a cookie is only intended to be accessed in a first party context, the developer has the option to apply one of settings {@code SameSite=Lax} or {@code SameSite=Strict} or {@code SameSite=None} to prevent external access.

To safeguard more websites and their users, the new secure-by-default model assumes all cookies should be protected from external access unless otherwise specified. Developers must use a new cookie setting, {@code SameSite=None}, to designate cookies for cross-site access. When the {@code SameSite=None} attribute is present, an additional {@code Secure} attribute is used so cross-site cookies can only be accessed over HTTPS connections.

Accepted values are:
  • {@code Lax}
  • {@code Strict}
  • {@code None}
  • {@code Off}: Disable the generation of the SameSite cookie attribute altogether.
  • Path to a Groovy script that is able to generate the SameSite cookie attribute dynamically.
  • Fully qualified name of a class that implements {@code org.apereo.cas.web.cookie.CookieSameSitePolicy}

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.csrf-cookie.secure
docs.description: True if sending this cookie should be restricted to a secure protocol, or false if the it can be sent using any protocol.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.device-token.max-time-to-live-in-seconds
docs.description: Hard timeout to kill the device token and expire it.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.device-token.refresh-interval
docs.description: The device refresh interval. The client should attempt to acquire an access token every few seconds (at a rate specified by interval) by POSTing to the access token endpoint on the server.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.device-token.storage-name
docs.description: The storage object name used and created by CAS to hold OAuth device tokens in the backing ticket registry implementation.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.device-user-code.max-time-to-live-in-seconds
docs.description: Hard timeout to kill the token and expire it.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.device-user-code.storage-name
docs.description: The storage object name used and created by CAS to hold OAuth device user codes in the backing ticket registry implementation.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.device-user-code.user-code-length
docs.description: Length of the generated user code.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.grants.resource-owner.require-service-header
docs.description: Whether using the resource-owner grant should enforce authorization rules and per-service policies based on a service parameter is provided as a header outside the normal semantics of the grant and protocol.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.refresh-token.create-as-jwt
docs.description: Create access token as JWTs.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.refresh-token.max-active-tokens-allowed
docs.description: Maximum number of active refresh tokens that an application can receive. If the application requests more that this limit, the request will be denied and the access token will not be issued.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.refresh-token.storage-name
docs.description: The storage object name used and created by CAS to hold OAuth refresh tokens in the backing ticket registry implementation.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.refresh-token.time-to-kill-in-seconds
docs.description: Hard timeout beyond which the refresh token is considered expired.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.refresh-token.track-access-tokens
docs.description: If true, the refresh token will keep track of the access tokens issued using it. The access tokens will remain attached to the refresh token as long as the refresh token is valid and they are not periodically on on-demand checked for validity or removed from the refresh token if they expire. The tracking mechanism is only for history and auditing purposes.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.cookie.allowed-ip-addresses-pattern
docs.description: A regular expression pattern that indicates the set of allowed IP addresses, when {@link #isPinToSession()} is configured. In the event that there is a mismatch between the cookie IP address and the current request-provided IP address (i.e. network switches, VPN, etc), the cookie can still be considered valid if the new IP address matches the pattern specified here.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.cookie.auto-configure-cookie-path
docs.description: Decide if cookie paths should be automatically configured based on the application context path, when the cookie path is not configured. @deprecated since 7.3.0

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.cookie.crypto.alg
docs.description: The signing/encryption algorithm to use.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.cookie.crypto.enabled
docs.description: Whether crypto operations are enabled.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.cookie.crypto.encryption.key
docs.description: The encryption key is a string whose length is defined by the encryption key size setting.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.cookie.crypto.encryption.key-size
docs.description: The encryption key size.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.cookie.crypto.signing.key
docs.description: The signing key is a string whose length is defined by the signing key size setting.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.cookie.crypto.signing.key-size
docs.description: The signing key size.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.cookie.crypto.strategy-type
docs.description:
Control the cipher sequence of operations. The accepted values are:
  • {@code ENCRYPT_AND_SIGN}: Encrypt the value first, and then sign.
  • {@code SIGN_AND_ENCRYPT}: Sign the value first, and then encrypt.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.cookie.domain
docs.description: Cookie domain. Specifies the domain within which this cookie should be presented. The form of the domain name is specified by RFC 2965. A domain name begins with a dot (.foo.com) and means that the cookie is visible to servers in a specified Domain Name System (DNS) zone (for example, www.foo.com, but not a.b.foo.com). By default, cookies are only returned to the server that sent them.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.cookie.geo-locate-client-session
docs.description: When set to {@code true} and assuming {@link #isPinToSession()} is also {@code true}, client sessions (using the client IP address) are geo-located using a geolocation service when/if configured. The resulting session is either pinned to the client geolocation, or the default client address.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.cookie.http-only
docs.description: true if this cookie contains the HttpOnly attribute. This means that the cookie should not be accessible to scripting engines, like javascript.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.cookie.max-age
docs.description: The maximum age of the cookie, specified in seconds. By default, {@code -1} indicating the cookie will persist until browser shutdown. A positive value indicates that the cookie will expire after that many seconds have passed. Note that the value is the maximum age when the cookie will expire, not the cookie's current age. A negative value means that the cookie is not stored persistently and will be deleted when the Web browser exits. A zero value causes the cookie to be deleted.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.cookie.name
docs.description: Cookie name. Constructs a cookie with a specified name and value. The name must conform to RFC 2965. That means it can contain only ASCII alphanumeric characters and cannot contain commas, semicolons, or white space or begin with a {@code $} character. The cookie's name cannot be changed after creation. By default, cookies are created according to the RFC 2965 cookie specification. Cookie names are automatically calculated assigned by CAS at runtime, and there is usually no need to customize the name or assign it a different value unless a special use case warrants the change.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.cookie.path
docs.description: Cookie path. Specifies a path for the cookie to which the client should return the cookie. The cookie is visible to all the pages in the directory you specify, and all the pages in that directory's subdirectories. A cookie's path must include the servlet that set the cookie, for example, /catalog, which makes the cookie visible to all directories on the server under /catalog. Consult RFC 2965 (available on the Internet) for more information on setting path names for cookies.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.cookie.pin-to-session
docs.description:
When generating cookie values, determine whether the value should be compounded and signed with the properties of the current session, such as IP address, user-agent, etc.

Turning off session pinning is not exactly ideal. This is a barrier to prevent cookie replay attacks. A cookie that was created with an IP given a certain location cannot be replayed back in a different browser with a different IP from a different location.

There may however be legitimate reasons to turn it off and relax this after careful reviews, if you intend to support a type of user who intends to switch their IP quite frequently. A classic example is the type of user that is on VPN at the time of login, but decides to resume their work a few hours later off VPN or at a different location.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.cookie.same-site-policy
docs.description:
If a cookie is only intended to be accessed in a first party context, the developer has the option to apply one of settings {@code SameSite=Lax} or {@code SameSite=Strict} or {@code SameSite=None} to prevent external access.

To safeguard more websites and their users, the new secure-by-default model assumes all cookies should be protected from external access unless otherwise specified. Developers must use a new cookie setting, {@code SameSite=None}, to designate cookies for cross-site access. When the {@code SameSite=None} attribute is present, an additional {@code Secure} attribute is used so cross-site cookies can only be accessed over HTTPS connections.

Accepted values are:
  • {@code Lax}
  • {@code Strict}
  • {@code None}
  • {@code Off}: Disable the generation of the SameSite cookie attribute altogether.
  • Path to a Groovy script that is able to generate the SameSite cookie attribute dynamically.
  • Fully qualified name of a class that implements {@code org.apereo.cas.web.cookie.CookieSameSitePolicy}

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.cookie.secure
docs.description: True if sending this cookie should be restricted to a secure protocol, or false if the it can be sent using any protocol.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.session-replication.replicate-sessions
docs.description: Indicates whether profiles and other session data, collected as part of authentication flows and protocol requests that are kept by the container session, should be replicated across the cluster using CAS and its own ticket registry. Without this option, profile data and other related pieces of information should be manually replicated via means and libraries outside of CAS. @deprecated since 7.3.0

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.core.issuer
docs.description: UMA issuer.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.permission-ticket.max-time-to-live-in-seconds
docs.description: Hard timeout to kill the UMA permission token and expire it.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.requesting-party-token.jwks-file.location
docs.description:
The location of the resource. Resources can be URLs, or files found either on the classpath or outside somewhere in the file system.

In the event the configured resource is a Groovy script, especially if the script is set to reload on changes, you may need to adjust the total number of {@code inotify} instances. On Linux, you may need to add the following line to {@code /etc/sysctl.conf}: {@code fs.inotify.max_user_instances = 256}.

You can check the current value via {@code cat /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances}.

In situations and scenarios where CAS is able to automatically watch the underlying resource for changes and detect updates and modifications dynamically, you may be able to specify the following setting as either an environment variable or system property with a value of {@code false} to disable the resource watcher: {@code org.apereo.cas.util.io.PathWatcherService}.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.requesting-party-token.max-time-to-live-in-seconds
docs.description: Hard timeout to kill the RP token and expire it.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.autocommit
docs.description: The default auto-commit behavior of connections in the pool. Determined whether queries such as update/insert should be immediately executed without waiting for an underlying transaction.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.batch-size
docs.description: A non-zero value enables use of JDBC2 batch updates by Hibernate. e.g. recommended values between 5 and 30.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.connection-timeout
docs.description: Indicates the maximum number of milliseconds that the service can wait to obtain a connection.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.data-source-name
docs.description: Attempts to do a JNDI data source look up for the data source name specified. Will attempt to locate the data source object as is.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.ddl-auto
docs.description:
Hibernate feature to automatically validate and exports DDL to the schema. By default, creates and drops the schema automatically when a session is starts and ends. Setting the value to {@code validate} or {@code none} may be more desirable for production, but any of the following options can be used:
  • {@code validate}: Validate the schema, but make no changes to the database.
  • {@code update}: Update the schema.
  • {@code create}: Create the schema, destroying previous data.
  • {@code create-drop}: Drop the schema at the end of the session.
  • {@code none}: Do nothing.

Note that during a version migration where any schema has changed {@code create-drop} will result in the loss of all data as soon as CAS is started. For transient data like tickets this is probably not an issue, but in cases like the audit table important data could be lost. Using `update`, while safe for data, is confirmed to result in invalid database state. {@code validate} or {@code none} settings are likely the only safe options for production use.

For more info, see this.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.default-catalog
docs.description: Qualifies unqualified table names with the given catalog in generated SQL.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.default-schema
docs.description: Qualify unqualified table names with the given schema/tablespace in generated SQL.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.dialect
docs.description: The database dialect is a configuration setting for platform independent software (JPA, Hibernate, etc) which allows such software to translate its generic SQL statements into vendor specific DDL, DML.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.driver-class
docs.description: The JDBC driver used to connect to the database.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.fail-fast-timeout
docs.description:
Set the pool initialization failure timeout.
  • Any value greater than zero will be treated as a timeout for pool initialization. The calling thread will be blocked from continuing until a successful connection to the database, or until the timeout is reached. If the timeout is reached, then a {@code PoolInitializationException} will be thrown.
  • A value of zero will not prevent the pool from starting in the case that a connection cannot be obtained. However, upon start the pool will attempt to obtain a connection and validate that the {@code connectionTestQuery} and {@code connectionInitSql} are valid. If those validations fail, an exception will be thrown. If a connection cannot be obtained, the validation is skipped and the pool will start and continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
  • A value less than zero will not bypass any connection attempt and validation during startup, and therefore the pool will start immediately. The pool will continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
Note that if this timeout value is greater than or equal to zero (0), and therefore an initial connection validation is performed, this timeout does not override the {@code connectionTimeout} or {@code validationTimeout}; they will be honored before this timeout is applied. The default value is one millisecond.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.fetch-size
docs.description: Used to specify number of rows to be fetched in a select query.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.generate-statistics
docs.description: Allow hibernate to generate query statistics.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.health-query
docs.description: The SQL query to be executed to test the validity of connections. This is for "legacy" databases that do not support the JDBC4 {@code Connection.isValid()} API.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.idle-timeout
docs.description: Controls the maximum amount of time that a connection is allowed to sit idle in the pool.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.isolate-internal-queries
docs.description:
This property determines whether data source isolates internal pool queries, such as the connection alive test, in their own transaction.

Since these are typically read-only queries, it is rarely necessary to encapsulate them in their own transaction. This property only applies if {@link #autocommit} is disabled.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.isolation-level-name
docs.description: Defines the isolation level for transactions. @see org.springframework.transaction.TransactionDefinition

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.leak-threshold
docs.description: Controls the amount of time that a connection can be out of the pool before a message is logged indicating a possible connection leak.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.password
docs.description: The database connection password.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.physical-naming-strategy-class-name
docs.description: Fully-qualified name of the class that can control the physical naming strategy of hibernate.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.pool.keep-alive-time
docs.description: This property controls the keepalive interval for a connection in the pool. An in-use connection will never be tested by the keepalive thread, only when it is idle will it be tested. Default is zero, which disables this feature.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.pool.max-size
docs.description: Controls the maximum number of connections to keep in the pool, including both idle and in-use connections.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.pool.max-wait
docs.description:
Sets the maximum time in seconds that this data source will wait while attempting to connect to a database.

A value of zero specifies that the timeout is the default system timeout if there is one; otherwise, it specifies that there is no timeout.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.pool.maximum-lifetime
docs.description: This property controls the maximum lifetime of a connection in the pool. When a connection reaches this timeout, even if recently used, it will be retired from the pool. An in-use connection will never be retired, only when it is idle will it be removed.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.pool.min-size
docs.description: Controls the minimum size that the pool is allowed to reach, including both idle and in-use connections.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.pool.name
docs.description: Set the name of the connection pool. This is primarily used for the MBean to uniquely identify the pool configuration.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.pool.suspension
docs.description:
Whether or not pool suspension is allowed.

There is a performance impact when pool suspension is enabled. Unless you need it (for a redundancy system for example) do not enable it.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.pool.timeout-millis
docs.description: The maximum number of milliseconds that the pool will wait for a connection to be validated as alive.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.propagation-behavior-name
docs.description: Defines the propagation behavior for transactions. @see org.springframework.transaction.TransactionDefinition

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.properties
docs.description: Additional settings provided by Hibernate (or the connection provider) in form of key-value pairs.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.read-only
docs.description: Configures the Connections to be added to the pool as read-only Connections.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.url
docs.description: The database connection URL.

docs.name: cas.authn.oauth.uma.resource-set.jpa.user
docs.description:
The database user.

The database user must have sufficient permissions to be able to handle schema changes and updates, when needed.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.ciba.max-time-to-live-in-seconds
docs.description: Hard timeout to kill the ID token and expire it.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.ciba.storage-name
docs.description: The storage object name used and created by CAS to hold CIBA requests in the backing ticket registry implementation.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.ciba.verification.delay
docs.description: Number of seconds to pause and wait before sending out the verification notification to the user. Essentially, this controls how long the user must wait before the notification message is received via email, etc.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.ciba.verification.mail.attribute-name
docs.description: Principal attribute names that indicates the destination email address for this message. The attributes must already be resolved and available to the CAS principal. When multiple attributes are specified, each attribute is then examined against the available CAS principal to locate the email address value, which may result in multiple emails being sent.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.ciba.verification.mail.bcc
docs.description: Email BCC address, if any.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.ciba.verification.mail.cc
docs.description: Email CC address, if any.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.ciba.verification.mail.from
docs.description: Email from address.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.ciba.verification.mail.html
docs.description: Indicate whether the message body should be evaluated as HTML text. The application of this setting depends on the email provider implementation and may not be fully supported everywhere. This is typically relevant for the default {@link org.springframework.mail.javamail.JavaMailSender}.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.ciba.verification.mail.priority
docs.description: Set the priority ({@code X-Priority} header) of the message. Values: {@code 1 (Highest)}, {@code 2 (High)}, {@code 3 (Normal)}, {@code 4 (Low)}, {@code 5 (Lowest)}. The application of this setting depends on the email provider implementation and may not be fully supported everywhere. This is typically relevant for the default {@link org.springframework.mail.javamail.JavaMailSender}.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.ciba.verification.mail.reply-to
docs.description: Email Reply-To address, if any.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.ciba.verification.mail.subject
docs.description:
Email subject line.

The subject can either be defined verbatim, or it may point to a message key in the language bundle using the syntax {@code #{subject-language-key}}. This key should point to a valid message defined in the appropriate language bundle that is then picked up via the active locale. In case where the language code cannot resolve the real subject, a default subject value would be used.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.ciba.verification.mail.text
docs.description:
Email message body. Could be plain text or a reference to an external file that would serve as a template.

If specified as a path to an external file with an extension {@code .gtemplate}, then the email message body would be processed using the Groovy template engine. The template engine uses JSP style <% %> script and <%= %> expression syntax or GString style expressions. The variable {@code out} is bound to the writer that the template is being written to.

If using plain text, the contents are processed for string substitution candidates using named variables. For example, you may refer to an expected url variable in the email text via {@code ${url}}, or use {@code ${token}} to locate the token variable. In certain cases, additional parameters are passed to the email body processor that might include authentication and/or principal attributes, the available locale, client http information, etc.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.ciba.verification.mail.validate-addresses
docs.description: Set whether to validate all addresses which get passed to this helper. The application of this setting depends on the email provider implementation and may not be fully supported everywhere. This is typically relevant for the default {@link org.springframework.mail.javamail.JavaMailSender}.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.core.accepted-issuers-pattern
docs.description: Defines the regular expression pattern that is matched against the calculated issuer from the request. If the issuer that is extracted from the request does not match the {@link #issuer} defined in the CAS configuration, this pattern acts as a secondary level rule to allow incoming requests to pass through if the match is successful. By default, the pattern is designed to never match anything.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.core.authentication-context-reference-mappings
docs.description:
A mapping of authentication context refs (ACR) values. This is where specific authentication context classes are referenced and mapped to providers that CAS may support mainly for MFA purposes.

Example might be {@code acr-value->mfa-duo}.

Support for authentication context class references is implemented in form of {@code acr_values} as part of the original authorization request, which is mostly taken into account by the multifactor authentication features of CAS. Once successful, {@code acr} and {@code amr} values are passed back to the relying party as part of the ID token.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.core.claims-map
docs.description: Map fixed claims to CAS attributes. Key is the existing claim name for a scope and value is the new attribute that should take its place and value. Claims associated with a scope (i.e. given_name for profile) are fixed in the OpenID specification. In the event that custom arbitrary attributes should be mapped to claims, mappings can be defined in CAS settings to link a CAS-defined attribute to a fixed given scope. For instance, CAS configuration may allow the value of the attribute {@code sys_given_name} to be mapped and assigned to the claim {@code given_name} without having an impact on the attribute resolution configuration and all other CAS-enabled applications. If mapping is not defined, by default CAS attributes are expected to match claim names.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.core.issuer
docs.description:
OIDC issuer. All OpenID Connect servers such as CAS are uniquely identified by a URL known as the issuer. This URL serves as the prefix of a service discovery endpoint as specified in the OpenID Connect Discovery standard.

This URL must be using the https scheme with no query or fragment component that the identity provider (CAS) asserts as its Issuer Identifier. This also MUST be identical to the {@code iss} claim value in ID Tokens issued from this issuer, unless overridden in very special circumstances as a last resort.

CAS primarily supports a single issuer per deployment/host.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.core.skew
docs.description: Skew value used to massage the authentication issue instance.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.core.user-defined-scopes
docs.description: Mapping of user-defined scopes. Key is the new scope name and value is a comma-separated list of claims mapped to the scope. Such user-defined scopes are also able to override the definition of system scopes. User-defined scopes as well as any and all custom claims that are mapped to the scope must also be defined as scopes and claims supported by CAS in OpenID Connect discovery.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.discovery.acr-values-supported
docs.description: List of ACR values supported. This discovery element contains a list of the supported acr values supported by this server. Support for authentication context class references is implemented in form of {@code acr_values} as part of the original authorization request, which is mostly taken into account by the multifactor authentication features of CAS. Once successful, {@code acr} and {@code amr} values are passed back to the relying party as part of the ID token.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.discovery.authorization-response-issuer-parameter-supported
docs.description: Parameter indicating whether the authorization server provides the {@code iss} parameter in the authorization response.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.discovery.backchannel-authentication-request-signing-alg-values-supported
docs.description: List of the JWS signing algorithms (alg values) supported by the CAS for signed authentication requests. If omitted, signed authentication requests are not supported by the CAS.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.discovery.backchannel-token-delivery-modes-supported
docs.description: Supported backchannel token delivery modes used for CIBA.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.discovery.backchannel-user-code-parameter-supported
docs.description: Boolean value specifying whether the OP supports the use of the {@code user_code} parameter.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.discovery.claim-types-supported
docs.description: Supported claim types.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.discovery.claims
docs.description: List of supported claims.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.discovery.claims-in-verified-claims-supported
docs.description: List of the supported verified claims.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.discovery.claims-parameter-supported
docs.description: Specifying whether this provider supports use of the claims parameter.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.discovery.code-challenge-methods-supported
docs.description: List of PKCE code challenge methods supported.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.discovery.documents-supported
docs.description: Needed when {@link #evidenceSupported} contains {@code document} or {@code id_document}. Set containing all identity document types utilized by the CAS for identity verification.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.discovery.documents-validation-methods-supported
docs.description: Set containing the validation methods the CAS supports.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.id-token.include-id-token-claims
docs.description:
As per OpenID Connect Core section 5.4, "The Claims requested by the {@code profile}, {@code email}, {@code address}, and {@code phone} scope values are returned from the userinfo endpoint", except for {@code response_type}={@code id_token}, where they are returned in the id_token (as there is no access token issued that could be used to access the userinfo endpoint). The Claims requested by the profile, email, address, and phone scope values are returned from the userinfo endpoint when a {@code response_type} value is used that results in an access token being issued. However, when no access token is issued (which is the case for the {@code response_type} value {@code id_token}), the resulting Claims are returned in the ID Token.

Setting this flag to true will force CAS to include claims in the ID token regardless of the response type. Note that this setting MUST ONLY be used as a last resort, to stay compliant with the specification as much as possible. DO NOT use this setting without due consideration.

Note that this setting is set to {@code true} by default mainly provided to preserve backward compatibility with previous CAS versions that included claims into the ID token without considering the response type. The behavior of this setting may change and it may be removed in future CAS releases.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.identity-assurance.verification-source.location
docs.description:
The location of the resource. Resources can be URLs, or files found either on the classpath or outside somewhere in the file system.

In the event the configured resource is a Groovy script, especially if the script is set to reload on changes, you may need to adjust the total number of {@code inotify} instances. On Linux, you may need to add the following line to {@code /etc/sysctl.conf}: {@code fs.inotify.max_user_instances = 256}.

You can check the current value via {@code cat /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances}.

In situations and scenarios where CAS is able to automatically watch the underlying resource for changes and detect updates and modifications dynamically, you may be able to specify the following setting as either an environment variable or system property with a value of {@code false} to disable the resource watcher: {@code org.apereo.cas.util.io.PathWatcherService}.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.jwks.jpa.ddl-auto
docs.description:
Hibernate feature to automatically validate and exports DDL to the schema. By default, creates and drops the schema automatically when a session is starts and ends. Setting the value to {@code validate} or {@code none} may be more desirable for production, but any of the following options can be used:
  • {@code validate}: Validate the schema, but make no changes to the database.
  • {@code update}: Update the schema.
  • {@code create}: Create the schema, destroying previous data.
  • {@code create-drop}: Drop the schema at the end of the session.
  • {@code none}: Do nothing.

Note that during a version migration where any schema has changed {@code create-drop} will result in the loss of all data as soon as CAS is started. For transient data like tickets this is probably not an issue, but in cases like the audit table important data could be lost. Using `update`, while safe for data, is confirmed to result in invalid database state. {@code validate} or {@code none} settings are likely the only safe options for production use.

For more info, see this.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.jwks.jpa.fail-fast-timeout
docs.description:
Set the pool initialization failure timeout.
  • Any value greater than zero will be treated as a timeout for pool initialization. The calling thread will be blocked from continuing until a successful connection to the database, or until the timeout is reached. If the timeout is reached, then a {@code PoolInitializationException} will be thrown.
  • A value of zero will not prevent the pool from starting in the case that a connection cannot be obtained. However, upon start the pool will attempt to obtain a connection and validate that the {@code connectionTestQuery} and {@code connectionInitSql} are valid. If those validations fail, an exception will be thrown. If a connection cannot be obtained, the validation is skipped and the pool will start and continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
  • A value less than zero will not bypass any connection attempt and validation during startup, and therefore the pool will start immediately. The pool will continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
Note that if this timeout value is greater than or equal to zero (0), and therefore an initial connection validation is performed, this timeout does not override the {@code connectionTimeout} or {@code validationTimeout}; they will be honored before this timeout is applied. The default value is one millisecond.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.registration.client-secret-expiration
docs.description: When client secret is issued by CAS, this is the period that gets added to the current time measured in UTC to determine the client secret's expiration date. An example value would be {@code P14D} forcing client applications to expire their client secret in 2 weeks after the registration date. Expired client secrets can be updated using the client configuration endpoint. A value of {@code 0} indicates that client secrets would never expire.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.registration.dynamic-client-registration-mode
docs.description:
Whether dynamic registration operates in {@code OPEN} or {@code PROTECTED} mode. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code OPEN}: Registration is open to all. In a situation where CAS is supporting open Client registration, it will check to see if the {@code logo_uri} and {@code policy_uri} have the same host as the hosts defined in the array of {@code redirect_uris}.
  • {@code PROTECTED}: registration is protected for all.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.registration.initial-access-token-password
docs.description: The password used in a basic-auth scheme to request an initial access token that would then be used to dynamically register clients in {@link DynamicClientRegistrationModes#PROTECTED} mode.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.registration.initial-access-token-user
docs.description: The username used in a basic-auth scheme to request an initial access token that would then be used to dynamically register clients in {@link DynamicClientRegistrationModes#PROTECTED} mode.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.response.crypto.enabled
docs.description: Whether crypto operations are enabled.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.response.crypto.encryption-enabled
docs.description: Whether crypto encryption operations are enabled.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.response.crypto.signing-enabled
docs.description: Whether crypto signing operations are enabled.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.response.crypto.strategy-type
docs.description:
Control the cipher sequence of operations. The accepted values are:
  • {@code ENCRYPT_AND_SIGN}: Encrypt the value first, and then sign.
  • {@code SIGN_AND_ENCRYPT}: Sign the value first, and then encrypt.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.services.defaults
docs.description: Control the default, initial values for fields that are part of a OIDC service definition. This is defined as a map where the key is the field name (i.e. {@code signIdToken}) and the value should be the default value. If a service definition explicitly defines a value for a field, that value will take over and the default defined here will be ignored. If a service definition does not define a value for a field and no defaults are specified for that field, then the default value that is directly assigned to the field in the body of the service definition will take over.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.webfinger.enabled
docs.description: Indicate if webfinger discovery protocol should be enabled.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.webfinger.resource-pattern
docs.description: The regular expression pattern to use to match against the resource URL.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.webfinger.user-info.groovy.location
docs.description:
The location of the resource. Resources can be URLs, or files found either on the classpath or outside somewhere in the file system.

In the event the configured resource is a Groovy script, especially if the script is set to reload on changes, you may need to adjust the total number of {@code inotify} instances. On Linux, you may need to add the following line to {@code /etc/sysctl.conf}: {@code fs.inotify.max_user_instances = 256}.

You can check the current value via {@code cat /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances}.

In situations and scenarios where CAS is able to automatically watch the underlying resource for changes and detect updates and modifications dynamically, you may be able to specify the following setting as either an environment variable or system property with a value of {@code false} to disable the resource watcher: {@code org.apereo.cas.util.io.PathWatcherService}.

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.webfinger.user-info.rest.headers

docs.name: cas.authn.oidc.webfinger.user-info.rest.method

docs.name: cas.authn.okta.credential-criteria
docs.description:
A number of authentication handlers are allowed to determine whether they can operate on the provided credential and as such lend themselves to be tried and tested during the authentication handler selection phase. The credential criteria may be one of the following options:
  • 1) A regular expression pattern that is tested against the credential identifier.
  • 2) A fully qualified class name of your own design that implements {@code Predicate}.
  • 3) Path to an external Groovy script that implements the same interface.

docs.name: cas.authn.okta.name

docs.name: cas.authn.okta.order

docs.name: cas.authn.okta.organization-url

docs.name: cas.authn.okta.password-encoder.character-encoding
docs.description: The encoding algorithm to use such as 'UTF-8'. Relevant when the type used is {@code DEFAULT}.

docs.name: cas.authn.okta.password-encoder.encoding-algorithm
docs.description: The encoding algorithm to use such as {@code MD5}. Relevant when the type used is {@code DEFAULT} or {@code GLIBC_CRYPT}. When used with {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#PBKDF2}, it should be one of {@code PBKDF2WithHmacSHA1}, {@code PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256} or {@code PBKDF2WithHmacSHA512}.

docs.name: cas.authn.okta.password-encoder.hash-length
docs.description: When used by {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#ARGON2}, it indicates the hash strength/length.

docs.name: cas.authn.okta.password-encoder.iterations
docs.description: When used by {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#PBKDF2}, it indicates the required number of iterations.

docs.name: cas.authn.okta.password-encoder.secret
docs.description: Secret to use with {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#STANDARD}, {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#PBKDF2}, {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#BCRYPT}, {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#GLIBC_CRYPT} password encoders. Secret usually is an optional setting.

docs.name: cas.authn.okta.password-encoder.strength
docs.description: Strength or number of iterations to use for password hashing. Usually relevant when dealing with {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#BCRYPT}, {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#PBKDF2} or {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#GLIBC_CRYPT}. When used by {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#ARGON2} or {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#PBKDF2}, it indicates the salt strength.

docs.name: cas.authn.okta.password-encoder.type
docs.description:
Define the password encoder type to use. Type may be specified as blank or {@code NONE} to disable password encoding. It may also refer to a fully-qualified class name that implements the Spring Security's {@code PasswordEncoder} interface if you wish you define your own encoder.

The following types may be used:

  • {@code NONE}: No password encoding (i.e. plain-text) takes place.
  • {@code DEFAULT}: Use the {@code DefaultPasswordEncoder} of CAS. For message-digest algorithms via {@code character-encoding} and {@code encoding-algorithm}.
  • {@code BCRYPT}: Use the {@code BCryptPasswordEncoder} based on the strength provided and an optional secret.
  • {@code SCRYPT}: Use the {@code SCryptPasswordEncoder}.
  • {@code PBKDF2}: Use the {@code Pbkdf2PasswordEncoder} based on the strength provided and an optional secret.
  • {@code STANDARD}: Use the {@code StandardPasswordEncoder} based on the secret provided.
  • {@code SSHA}: Use the {@code LdapShaPasswordEncoder} supports Ldap SHA and SSHA (salted-SHA). The values are base-64 encoded and have the label {SHA} or {SSHA} prepended to the encoded hash.
  • {@code GLIBC_CRYPT}: Use the {@code GlibcCryptPasswordEncoder} based on the {@code encoding-algorithm}, strength provided and an optional secret.
  • {@code org.example.MyEncoder}: An implementation of {@code PasswordEncoder} of your own choosing.
  • {@code file:///path/to/script.groovy}: Path to a Groovy script charged with handling password encoding operations.

docs.name: cas.authn.okta.provisioning.attribute-mappings
docs.description: Map of attributes that optionally may be used to control the names of the attributes to Okta that form the user profile. If an attribute is provided by Okta, such as {@code department}, it can be listed here as the key of the map with a value that should be the name of that attribute as collected and recorded by CAS. For example, the convention {@code department->organization} will process the CAS attribute {@code organization} and will assign its value to the user profile under {@code department}. docs.name: cas.authn.okta.state
docs.description:
Define the scope and state of this authentication handler and the lifecycle in which it can be invoked or activated. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code ACTIVE}: Active authentication handler, and is invoked by default automatically to verify credentials globally.
  • {@code STANDBY}: Authentication handler is in a semi-enabled state, waiting to be called only on-demand when explicitly asked for.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.bitbucket.auto-redirect-type
docs.description:
Auto-redirect to this client. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code SERVER}: Redirect on the server side, typically making CAS invisible.
  • {@code CLIENT}: Redirect on the client side using browser redirects, etc.
  • {@code NONE}: Do nothing and let the selection take place manually.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.bitbucket.callback-url
docs.description: Callback URL to use to return the flow back to the CAS server one the identity provider is successfully done. This may be used at the discretion of the client and its type to build service parameters, redirect URIs, etc. If none is specified, the CAS server's login endpoint will be used as the basis of the final callback url.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.bitbucket.callback-url-type
docs.description:
Determine how the callback url should be resolved. Default is {@link CallbackUrlTypes#QUERY_PARAMETER}. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code PATH_PARAMETER}: Path parameter callback url. The client name is added to the path of the callback URL.
  • {@code QUERY_PARAMETER}: Query parameter callback url. The client name is added to the path of a query parameter.
  • {@code NONE}: No callback url. No name is added to the callback URL to be able to distinguish the client.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.bitbucket.client-name
docs.description: Name of the client mostly for UI purposes and uniqueness. This name, with 'non-word' characters converted to '-' (e.g. "This Org (New)" becomes "This-Org--New-") is added to the "class" attribute of the redirect link on the login page, to allow for custom styling of individual IdPs (e.g. for an organization logo).

docs.description: Decide if cookie paths should be automatically configured based on the application context path, when the cookie path is not configured.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.cookie.domain
docs.description: Cookie domain. Specifies the domain within which this cookie should be presented. The form of the domain name is specified by RFC 2965. A domain name begins with a dot (.foo.com) and means that the cookie is visible to servers in a specified Domain Name System (DNS) zone (for example, www.foo.com, but not a.b.foo.com). By default, cookies are only returned to the server that sent them.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.cookie.enabled
docs.description: Determine whether cookie settings should be enabled to track delegated authentication choices and identity providers.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.cookie.http-only
docs.description: true if this cookie contains the HttpOnly attribute. This means that the cookie should not be accessible to scripting engines, like javascript.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.cookie.max-age
docs.description: The maximum age of the cookie, specified in seconds. By default, {@code -1} indicating the cookie will persist until browser shutdown. A positive value indicates that the cookie will expire after that many seconds have passed. Note that the value is the maximum age when the cookie will expire, not the cookie's current age. A negative value means that the cookie is not stored persistently and will be deleted when the Web browser exits. A zero value causes the cookie to be deleted.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.cookie.name
docs.description: Cookie name. Constructs a cookie with a specified name and value. The name must conform to RFC 2965. That means it can contain only ASCII alphanumeric characters and cannot contain commas, semicolons, or white space or begin with a {@code $} character. The cookie's name cannot be changed after creation. By default, cookies are created according to the RFC 2965 cookie specification. Cookie names are automatically calculated assigned by CAS at runtime, and there is usually no need to customize the name or assign it a different value unless a special use case warrants the change.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.cookie.path
docs.description: Cookie path. Specifies a path for the cookie to which the client should return the cookie. The cookie is visible to all the pages in the directory you specify, and all the pages in that directory's subdirectories. A cookie's path must include the servlet that set the cookie, for example, /catalog, which makes the cookie visible to all directories on the server under /catalog. Consult RFC 2965 (available on the Internet) for more information on setting path names for cookies.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.cookie.same-site-policy
docs.description:
If a cookie is only intended to be accessed in a first party context, the developer has the option to apply one of settings {@code SameSite=Lax} or {@code SameSite=Strict} or {@code SameSite=None} to prevent external access.

To safeguard more websites and their users, the new secure-by-default model assumes all cookies should be protected from external access unless otherwise specified. Developers must use a new cookie setting, {@code SameSite=None}, to designate cookies for cross-site access. When the {@code SameSite=None} attribute is present, an additional {@code Secure} attribute is used so cross-site cookies can only be accessed over HTTPS connections.

Accepted values are:
  • {@code Lax}
  • {@code Strict}
  • {@code None}
  • {@code Off}: Disable the generation of the SameSite cookie attribute altogether.
  • Path to a Groovy script that is able to generate the SameSite cookie attribute dynamically.
  • Fully qualified name of a class that implements {@code org.apereo.cas.web.cookie.CookieSameSitePolicy}

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.cookie.secure
docs.description: True if sending this cookie should be restricted to a secure protocol, or false if the it can be sent using any protocol.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.core.cache-duration
docs.description: Control the expiration policy of the cache that holds onto the results.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.core.cache-size
docs.description:
Control the size of the delegated identity provider cache that holds identity providers.

This setting specifies the maximum number of entries the cache may contain. Note that the cache may evict an entry before this limit is exceeded or temporarily exceed the threshold while evicting. As the cache size grows close to the maximum, the cache evicts entries that are less likely to be used again. For example, the cache may evict an entry because it hasn't been used recently or very often.

In the event that there is a mismatch between the cookie IP address and the current request-provided IP address (i.e. network switches, VPN, etc), the cookie can still be considered valid if the new IP address matches the pattern specified here.

docs.description: Whether crypto operations are enabled.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.core.session-replication.cookie.crypto.encryption.key
docs.description: The encryption key is a string whose length is defined by the encryption key size setting.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.core.session-replication.cookie.crypto.encryption.key-size
docs.description: The encryption key size.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.core.session-replication.cookie.crypto.signing.key
docs.description: The signing key is a string whose length is defined by the signing key size setting.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.core.session-replication.cookie.crypto.signing.key-size
docs.description: The signing key size.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.core.session-replication.cookie.crypto.strategy-type
docs.description:
Control the cipher sequence of operations. The accepted values are:
  • {@code ENCRYPT_AND_SIGN}: Encrypt the value first, and then sign.
  • {@code SIGN_AND_ENCRYPT}: Sign the value first, and then encrypt.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.core.session-replication.cookie.domain
docs.description: Cookie domain. Specifies the domain within which this cookie should be presented. The form of the domain name is specified by RFC 2965. A domain name begins with a dot (.foo.com) and means that the cookie is visible to servers in a specified Domain Name System (DNS) zone (for example, www.foo.com, but not a.b.foo.com). By default, cookies are only returned to the server that sent them.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.core.session-replication.cookie.geo-locate-client-session
docs.description: When set to {@code true} and assuming {@link #isPinToSession()} is also {@code true}, client sessions (using the client IP address) are geo-located using a geolocation service when/if configured. The resulting session is either pinned to the client geolocation, or the default client address.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.core.session-replication.cookie.http-only
docs.description: true if this cookie contains the HttpOnly attribute. This means that the cookie should not be accessible to scripting engines, like javascript.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.core.session-replication.cookie.max-age
docs.description: The maximum age of the cookie, specified in seconds. By default, {@code -1} indicating the cookie will persist until browser shutdown. A positive value indicates that the cookie will expire after that many seconds have passed. Note that the value is the maximum age when the cookie will expire, not the cookie's current age. A negative value means that the cookie is not stored persistently and will be deleted when the Web browser exits. A zero value causes the cookie to be deleted.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.core.session-replication.cookie.name
docs.description: Cookie name. Constructs a cookie with a specified name and value. The name must conform to RFC 2965. That means it can contain only ASCII alphanumeric characters and cannot contain commas, semicolons, or white space or begin with a {@code $} character. The cookie's name cannot be changed after creation. By default, cookies are created according to the RFC 2965 cookie specification. Cookie names are automatically calculated assigned by CAS at runtime, and there is usually no need to customize the name or assign it a different value unless a special use case warrants the change.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.core.session-replication.cookie.path
docs.description: Cookie path. Specifies a path for the cookie to which the client should return the cookie. The cookie is visible to all the pages in the directory you specify, and all the pages in that directory's subdirectories. A cookie's path must include the servlet that set the cookie, for example, /catalog, which makes the cookie visible to all directories on the server under /catalog. Consult RFC 2965 (available on the Internet) for more information on setting path names for cookies.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.core.session-replication.cookie.pin-to-session
docs.description:
When generating cookie values, determine whether the value should be compounded and signed with the properties of the current session, such as IP address, user-agent, etc.

Turning off session pinning is not exactly ideal. This is a barrier to prevent cookie replay attacks. A cookie that was created with an IP given a certain location cannot be replayed back in a different browser with a different IP from a different location.

There may however be legitimate reasons to turn it off and relax this after careful reviews, if you intend to support a type of user who intends to switch their IP quite frequently. A classic example is the type of user that is on VPN at the time of login, but decides to resume their work a few hours later off VPN or at a different location.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.core.session-replication.cookie.same-site-policy
docs.description:
If a cookie is only intended to be accessed in a first party context, the developer has the option to apply one of settings {@code SameSite=Lax} or {@code SameSite=Strict} or {@code SameSite=None} to prevent external access.

To safeguard more websites and their users, the new secure-by-default model assumes all cookies should be protected from external access unless otherwise specified. Developers must use a new cookie setting, {@code SameSite=None}, to designate cookies for cross-site access. When the {@code SameSite=None} attribute is present, an additional {@code Secure} attribute is used so cross-site cookies can only be accessed over HTTPS connections.

Accepted values are:
  • {@code Lax}
  • {@code Strict}
  • {@code None}
  • {@code Off}: Disable the generation of the SameSite cookie attribute altogether.
  • Path to a Groovy script that is able to generate the SameSite cookie attribute dynamically.
  • Fully qualified name of a class that implements {@code org.apereo.cas.web.cookie.CookieSameSitePolicy}

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.core.session-replication.cookie.secure
docs.description: True if sending this cookie should be restricted to a secure protocol, or false if the it can be sent using any protocol.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.core.session-replication.replicate-sessions
docs.description: Indicates whether profiles and other session data, collected as part of authentication flows and protocol requests that are kept by the container session, should be replicated across the cluster using CAS and its own ticket registry. Without this option, profile data and other related pieces of information should be manually replicated via means and libraries outside of CAS. @deprecated since 7.3.0

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.batch-size
docs.description: A non-zero value enables use of JDBC2 batch updates by Hibernate. e.g. recommended values between 5 and 30.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.connection-timeout
docs.description: Indicates the maximum number of milliseconds that the service can wait to obtain a connection.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.data-source-name
docs.description: Attempts to do a JNDI data source look up for the data source name specified. Will attempt to locate the data source object as is.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.ddl-auto
docs.description:
Hibernate feature to automatically validate and exports DDL to the schema. By default, creates and drops the schema automatically when a session is starts and ends. Setting the value to {@code validate} or {@code none} may be more desirable for production, but any of the following options can be used:
  • {@code validate}: Validate the schema, but make no changes to the database.
  • {@code update}: Update the schema.
  • {@code create}: Create the schema, destroying previous data.
  • {@code create-drop}: Drop the schema at the end of the session.
  • {@code none}: Do nothing.

Note that during a version migration where any schema has changed {@code create-drop} will result in the loss of all data as soon as CAS is started. For transient data like tickets this is probably not an issue, but in cases like the audit table important data could be lost. Using `update`, while safe for data, is confirmed to result in invalid database state. {@code validate} or {@code none} settings are likely the only safe options for production use.

For more info, see this.

docs.description: Qualifies unqualified table names with the given catalog in generated SQL.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.default-schema
docs.description: Qualify unqualified table names with the given schema/tablespace in generated SQL.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.dialect
docs.description: The database dialect is a configuration setting for platform independent software (JPA, Hibernate, etc) which allows such software to translate its generic SQL statements into vendor specific DDL, DML.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.driver-class
docs.description: The JDBC driver used to connect to the database.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.fail-fast-timeout
docs.description:
Set the pool initialization failure timeout.
  • Any value greater than zero will be treated as a timeout for pool initialization. The calling thread will be blocked from continuing until a successful connection to the database, or until the timeout is reached. If the timeout is reached, then a {@code PoolInitializationException} will be thrown.
  • A value of zero will not prevent the pool from starting in the case that a connection cannot be obtained. However, upon start the pool will attempt to obtain a connection and validate that the {@code connectionTestQuery} and {@code connectionInitSql} are valid. If those validations fail, an exception will be thrown. If a connection cannot be obtained, the validation is skipped and the pool will start and continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
  • A value less than zero will not bypass any connection attempt and validation during startup, and therefore the pool will start immediately. The pool will continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
Note that if this timeout value is greater than or equal to zero (0), and therefore an initial connection validation is performed, this timeout does not override the {@code connectionTimeout} or {@code validationTimeout}; they will be honored before this timeout is applied. The default value is one millisecond.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.fetch-size

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.generate-statistics
docs.description: Allow hibernate to generate query statistics.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.health-query
docs.description: The SQL query to be executed to test the validity of connections. This is for "legacy" databases that do not support the JDBC4 {@code Connection.isValid()} API.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.idle-timeout
docs.description: Controls the maximum amount of time that a connection is allowed to sit idle in the pool.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.isolate-internal-queries
docs.description:
This property determines whether data source isolates internal pool queries, such as the connection alive test, in their own transaction.

Since these are typically read-only queries, it is rarely necessary to encapsulate them in their own transaction. This property only applies if {@link #autocommit} is disabled.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.isolation-level-name
docs.description: Defines the isolation level for transactions. @see org.springframework.transaction.TransactionDefinition

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.leak-threshold
docs.description: Controls the amount of time that a connection can be out of the pool before a message is logged indicating a possible connection leak.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.password

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.pool.keep-alive-time

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.pool.max-size

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.pool.max-wait
docs.description:
Sets the maximum time in seconds that this data source will wait while attempting to connect to a database.

A value of zero specifies that the timeout is the default system timeout if there is one; otherwise, it specifies that there is no timeout.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.pool.maximum-lifetime
docs.description: This property controls the maximum lifetime of a connection in the pool. When a connection reaches this timeout, even if recently used, it will be retired from the pool. An in-use connection will never be retired, only when it is idle will it be removed.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.pool.min-size

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.pool.name

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.pool.suspension
docs.description:

There is a performance impact when pool suspension is enabled. Unless you need it (for a redundancy system for example) do not enable it.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.jdbc.pool.timeout-millis

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.oauth2[].profile-attrs
docs.description: Profile attributes to request and collect in form of key-value pairs. Key is the attribute name, and value is the mapped attribute name, if necessary. If remapping is not required, key and value should match. It's also possible to define values as {@code CONVERTER|mapped-attribute}. {@code CONVERTER} should be the attribute converter specified by its acceptable type and when acceptable, the converter attempts to transform the provided attribute value. CAS can also provide a special attribute converter that does the transformation and conversion based on an inline groovy script. This special groovy converter can be specified using this example syntax for the value, {@code groovy { return attribute + '-test'}|mapped-attribute}.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.groovy.location
docs.description:
The location of the resource. Resources can be URLs, or files found either on the classpath or outside somewhere in the file system.

In the event the configured resource is a Groovy script, especially if the script is set to reload on changes, you may need to adjust the total number of {@code inotify} instances. On Linux, you may need to add the following line to {@code /etc/sysctl.conf}: {@code fs.inotify.max_user_instances = 256}.

You can check the current value via {@code cat /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances}.

In situations and scenarios where CAS is able to automatically watch the underlying resource for changes and detect updates and modifications dynamically, you may be able to specify the following setting as either an environment variable or system property with a value of {@code false} to disable the resource watcher: {@code org.apereo.cas.util.io.PathWatcherService}.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.ldap
docs.description: Connect to LDAP servers to locate candidate profiles for delegated authn.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.ldap[].allow-multiple-dns
docs.description:
Whether search/query results are allowed to match on multiple DNs,
or whether a single unique DN is expected for the result.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.ldap[].allow-multiple-entries
docs.description: Set if multiple Entries are allowed.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.ldap[].attributes
docs.description:
List of attributes that should be retrieved from LDAP
for this profile.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.ldap[].base-dn
docs.description:
Base DN to use.
There may be scenarios where different parts of a single LDAP tree could be considered as base-dns. Rather than duplicating
the LDAP configuration block for each individual base-dn, each entry can be specified
and joined together using a special delimiter character. The user DN is retrieved using the combination of all base-dn and DN
resolvers in the order defined. DN resolution should fail if multiple DNs are found. Otherwise the first DN found is returned.
Usual syntax is: {@code subtreeA,dc=example,dc=net|subtreeC,dc=example,dc=net}.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.ldap[].binary-attributes
docs.description:
Indicate the collection of attributes that are to be tagged and processed as binary
attributes by the underlying search resolver.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.ldap[].bind-credential
docs.description: The bind credential to use when connecting to LDAP.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.ldap[].bind-dn
docs.description:
The bind DN to use when connecting to LDAP. LDAP connection configuration injected into the LDAP connection pool can be initialized with the following parameters:
  • {@code bindDn/bindCredential} provided - Use the provided credentials to bind when initializing connections.
  • {@code bindDn/bindCredential} set to {@code *} - Use a fast-bind strategy to initialize the pool.
  • {@code bindDn/bindCredential} set to blank - Skip connection initializing; perform operations anonymously.
  • SASL mechanism provided - Use the given SASL mechanism to bind when initializing connections.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.ldap[].block-wait-time
docs.description:
The length of time the pool will block.
By default the pool will block indefinitely and there is no guarantee that
waiting threads will be serviced in the order in which they made their request.
This option should be used with a blocking connection pool when you need to control the exact
number of connections that can be created

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.ldap[].connect-timeout
docs.description: Sets the maximum amount of time that connects will block.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.ldap[].connection-strategy
docs.description:
If multiple URLs are provided as the ldapURL this describes how each URL will be processed.
  • {@code ACTIVE_PASSIVE} First LDAP will be used for every request unless it fails and then the next shall be used.
  • {@code ROUND_ROBIN} For each new connection the next url in the list will be used.
  • {@code RANDOM} For each new connection a random LDAP url will be selected.
  • {@code DNS_SRV} LDAP urls based on DNS SRV records of the configured/given LDAP url will be used.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.ldap[].disable-pooling
docs.description: Whether to use a pooled connection factory in components.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.ldap[].fail-fast
docs.description:
Attempt to populate the connection pool early on startup
and fail quickly if something goes wrong.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.ldap[].follow-referrals
docs.description: Set if search referrals should be followed.

Hostname verification options. Available values are as follows:

  • {@code ANY}: Skip hostname verification and allow all.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.ldap[].pool-passivator
docs.description:
You may receive unexpected LDAP failures, when CAS is configured to authenticate using {@code DIRECT} or {@code AUTHENTICATED} types and LDAP is locked down to not allow anonymous binds/searches. Every second attempt with a given LDAP connection from the pool would fail if it was on the same connection as a failed login attempt, and the regular connection validator would similarly fail. When a connection is returned back to a pool, it still may contain the principal and credentials from the previous attempt. Before the next bind attempt using that connection, the validator tries to validate the connection again but fails because it’s no longer trying with the configured bind credentials but with whatever user DN was used in the previous step. Given the validation failure, the connection is closed and CAS would deny access by default. Passivators attempt to reconnect to LDAP with the configured bind credentials, effectively resetting the connection to what it should be after each bind request. Furthermore if you are seeing errors in the logs that resemble a 'Operation exception encountered, reopening connection' type of message, this usually is an indication that the connection pool’s validation timeout established and created by CAS is greater than the timeout configured in the LDAP server, or more likely, in the load balancer in front of the LDAP servers. You can adjust the LDAP server session’s timeout for connections, or you can teach CAS to use a validity period that is equal or less than the LDAP server session’s timeout. Accepted values are:
  • {@code NONE}: No passivation takes place.
  • {@code BIND}: The default behavior which passivates a connection by performing a bind operation on it. This option requires the availability of bind credentials when establishing connections to LDAP.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.ldap[].profile-id-attribute
docs.description:
User attribute from LDAP that determines the identifier
of the linked profile.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.ldap[].prune-period

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.profile-selection.ldap[].search-entry-handlers.type
docs.description:
The type of search entry handler to choose. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code FOLLOW_SEARCH_REFERRAL}: Provides handling of an ldap referral for search operations.
  • {@code FOLLOW_SEARCH_RESULT_REFERENCE}: Provides handling of an ldap continuation reference for search operations.
  • {@code ACTIVE_DIRECTORY}: Process the entry results fetched from active directory and check for account status controls for disabled/expired accounts, etc.
  • {@code OBJECT_GUID}: Object guid search entry handler. Handles the {@code objectGUID} attribute fetching and conversion.
  • {@code OBJECT_SID}: Object sid search entry handler. Handles the {@code objectSid} attribute fetching and conversion.
  • {@code CASE_CHANGE}: Case change search entry handler. Provides the ability to modify the case of search entry DNs, attribute names, and attribute values.
  • {@code DN_ATTRIBUTE_ENTRY}: DN attribute entry handler. Adds the entry DN as an attribute to the result set. Provides a client side implementation of RFC 5020.
  • {@code MERGE}: Merge search entry handler. Merges the values of one or more attributes into a single attribute.
  • {@code PRIMARY_GROUP}: Primary group search handler. Constructs the primary group SID and then searches for that group and puts it's DN in the {@code memberOf} attribute of the original search entry.
  • {@code RANGE_ENTRY}: Range entry search handler. Rewrites attributes returned from Active Directory to include all values by performing additional searches.
  • {@code RECURSIVE_ENTRY}: Recursive entry search handler. This recursively searches based on a supplied attribute and merges those results into the original entry.
  • {@code MERGE_ENTRIES}: Merge entries handler. Merges the values of one or more attributes in all entries into a single attribute. The merged attribute may or may not already exist on the entry. If it does exist it's existing values will remain intact.

In the event the configured resource is a Groovy script, especially if the script is set to reload on changes, you may need to adjust the total number of {@code inotify} instances. On Linux, you may need to add the following line to {@code /etc/sysctl.conf}: {@code fs.inotify.max_user_instances = 256}.

You can check the current value via {@code cat /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances}.

In situations and scenarios where CAS is able to automatically watch the underlying resource for changes and detect updates and modifications dynamically, you may be able to specify the following setting as either an environment variable or system property with a value of {@code false} to disable the resource watcher: {@code org.apereo.cas.util.io.PathWatcherService}.

An example might be to fetch {@code givenName} from credential and rename it to {@code urn:oid:2.5.4.42} or vice versa.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].maximum-authentication-lifetime

Once you have an authenticated session on the identity provider, usually it won't prompt you again to enter your
credentials and it will automatically generate a new assertion for you. By default, the SAML client
will accept assertions based on a previous authentication for one hour.
You can adjust this behavior by modifying this setting. The unit of time here is seconds.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].message-store-factory
docs.description:
Factory implementing this interface provides services for storing and retrieval of SAML messages for e.g. verification of retrieved responses. The default factory is an always empty store. You may choose {@code org.pac4j.saml.store.HttpSessionStore} instead which allows SAML messages to be stored in a distributed session store especially required for high availability deployments and validation operations.

Available options are:

  • {@code EMPTY}: Uses the {@code EmptyStoreFactory}
  • {@code SESSION}: Uses the {@code HttpSessionStore}
  • Fully-qualified class name of the message store implementation.

Also note that the message store implementation can be supplied and configured at runtime as a Spring {@code @Bean} with the type {@code SAMLMessageStoreFactory} which, if found in the available application context, will override all other options.
