docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.ddl-auto
docs.description:
Hibernate feature to automatically validate and exports DDL to the schema. By default, creates and drops the schema automatically when a session is starts and ends. Setting the value to {@code validate} or {@code none} may be more desirable for production, but any of the following options can be used:
  • {@code validate}: Validate the schema, but make no changes to the database.
  • {@code update}: Update the schema.
  • {@code create}: Create the schema, destroying previous data.
  • {@code create-drop}: Drop the schema at the end of the session.
  • {@code none}: Do nothing.

Note that during a version migration where any schema has changed {@code create-drop} will result in the loss of all data as soon as CAS is started. For transient data like tickets this is probably not an issue, but in cases like the audit table important data could be lost. Using `update`, while safe for data, is confirmed to result in invalid database state. {@code validate} or {@code none} settings are likely the only safe options for production use.

For more info, see this.

docs.description:

which allows such software to translate its generic SQL statements into vendor specific DDL, DML.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.driver-class

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.fail-fast-timeout
docs.description:
Set the pool initialization failure timeout.
  • Any value greater than zero will be treated as a timeout for pool initialization. The calling thread will be blocked from continuing until a successful connection to the database, or until the timeout is reached. If the timeout is reached, then a {@code PoolInitializationException} will be thrown.
  • A value of zero will not prevent the pool from starting in the case that a connection cannot be obtained. However, upon start the pool will attempt to obtain a connection and validate that the {@code connectionTestQuery} and {@code connectionInitSql} are valid. If those validations fail, an exception will be thrown. If a connection cannot be obtained, the validation is skipped and the pool will start and continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
  • A value less than zero will not bypass any connection attempt and validation during startup, and therefore the pool will start immediately. The pool will continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
Note that if this timeout value is greater than or equal to zero (0), and therefore an initial connection validation is performed, this timeout does not override the {@code connectionTimeout} or {@code validationTimeout}; they will be honored before this timeout is applied. The default value is one millisecond.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.generate-statistics
docs.description: Allow hibernate to generate query statistics.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.health-query
docs.description:
The SQL query to be executed to test the validity of connections.
This is for "legacy" databases that do not support the JDBC4 {@code Connection.isValid()} API.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.idle-timeout
docs.description: Controls the maximum amount of time that a connection is allowed to sit idle in the pool.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.isolate-internal-queries
docs.description:
This property determines whether data source isolates internal pool queries, such as the connection alive test, in their own transaction.

Since these are typically read-only queries, it is rarely necessary to encapsulate them in their own transaction. This property only applies if {@link #autocommit} is disabled.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.isolation-level-name
docs.description: Defines the isolation level for transactions.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.leak-threshold
docs.description:
Controls the amount of time that a connection can be out of the pool before a message
is logged indicating a possible connection leak.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.password
docs.description: The database connection password.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.physical-naming-strategy-class-name
docs.description: Fully-qualified name of the class that can control the physical naming strategy of hibernate.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.pool.keep-alive-time
docs.description:
This property controls the keepalive interval for a connection in the pool. An in-use connection
will never be tested by the keepalive thread, only when it is idle will it be tested.
Default is zero, which disables this feature.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.pool.max-size
docs.description:
Controls the maximum number of connections to keep
in the pool, including both idle and in-use connections.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.pool.max-wait
docs.description:
Sets the maximum time in seconds that this data source will wait while attempting to connect to a database.

A value of zero specifies that the timeout is the default system timeout if there is one; otherwise, it specifies that there is no timeout.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.pool.maximum-lifetime
docs.description:
This property controls the maximum lifetime of a connection in the pool. When a connection
reaches this timeout, even if recently used,
it will be retired from the pool. An in-use connection will never be retired, only when it is idle will it be removed.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.pool.min-size
docs.description:
Controls the minimum size that the pool is allowed
to reach, including both idle and in-use connections.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.pool.name
docs.description:
Set the name of the connection pool. This is primarily used for
the MBean to uniquely identify the pool configuration.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.pool.suspension
docs.description:
Whether or not pool suspension is allowed.

There is a performance impact when pool suspension is enabled. Unless you need it (for a redundancy system for example) do not enable it.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.pool.timeout-millis
docs.description:
The maximum number of milliseconds that the
pool will wait for a connection to be validated as alive.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.propagation-behavior-name
docs.description: Defines the propagation behavior for transactions.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.properties
docs.description: Additional settings provided by Hibernate (or the connection provider) in form of key-value pairs.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.read-only
docs.description: Configures the Connections to be added to the pool as read-only Connections.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.table-name
docs.description:
The table name in the database that holds the SAML2 service provider metadata. The table structure and columns must be created and exist beforehand, and must match the following SQL statements, with expected adjustments depending on database type, driver and dialect:

{@code CREATE TABLE sp_metadata (entityId VARCHAR(512), metadata TEXT)}

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.url
docs.description: The database connection URL.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.jdbc.user
docs.description:
The database user.

The database user must have sufficient permissions to be able to handle schema changes and updates, when needed.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.authentication-database-name
docs.description: Name of the database to use for authentication.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.client-uri
docs.description:
The connection uri to the mongodb instance.
This typically takes on the form of {@code mongodb://user:psw@ds135522.somewhere.com:35522/db}.
If not specified, will fallback onto other individual settings.
If specified, takes over all other settings where applicable.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.collection
docs.description: MongoDb database collection name to fetch and/or create.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.database-name
docs.description: MongoDb database instance name.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.drop-collection
docs.description: Whether collections should be dropped on startup and re-created.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.host
docs.description:
MongoDb database host for authentication.
Multiple host addresses may be defined, separated by comma.
If more than one host is defined, it is assumed that each host contains the port as well, if any.
Otherwise the configuration may fallback onto the port defined.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.password
docs.description: MongoDb database password for authentication.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.pool.idle-time
docs.description:
The maximum idle time of a pooled connection.  A zero value indicates no limit
to the idle time.  A pooled connection that has
exceeded its idle time will be closed and replaced when necessary by a new connection.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.pool.life-time
docs.description:
The maximum time a pooled connection can live for.  A zero value indicates no limit
to the life time.  A pooled connection that
has exceeded its life time will be closed and replaced when necessary by a new connection.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.pool.max-size
docs.description: Maximum number of connections to keep around.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.pool.max-wait-time
docs.description: The maximum time that a thread may wait for a connection to become available.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.pool.min-size
docs.description: Minimum number of connections to keep around.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.pool.per-host
docs.description: Total number of connections allowed per host.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.port
docs.description: MongoDb database port.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.read-concern
docs.description:
Read concern. Accepted values are:
  • {@code LOCAL}
  • {@code MAJORITY}
  • {@code LINEARIZABLE}
  • {@code SNAPSHOT}
  • {@code AVAILABLE}

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.read-preference
docs.description:
Read preference. Accepted values are:
  • {@code PRIMARY}
  • {@code SECONDARY}
  • {@code SECONDARY_PREFERRED}
  • {@code PRIMARY_PREFERRED}
  • {@code NEAREST}

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.replica-set
docs.description:
A replica set in MongoDB is a group of {@code mongod} processes that maintain
the same data set. Replica sets provide redundancy and high availability, and are the basis for all production deployments.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.retry-writes
docs.description: Sets whether writes should be retried if they fail due to a network error.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.socket-keep-alive
docs.description: Whether the database socket connection should be tagged with keep-alive.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.ssl-enabled
docs.description: Whether connections require SSL.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.timeout
docs.description: MongoDb database connection timeout.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.user-id
docs.description: MongoDb database user for authentication.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].metadata.service-provider.mongo.write-concern
docs.description:
Write concern describes the level of acknowledgement requested from
MongoDB for write operations to a standalone
mongo db or to replica sets or to sharded clusters. In sharded clusters,
mongo db instances will pass the write concern on to the shards.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].name-id-attribute
docs.description:
The attribute name that should be used and extracted from the SAML2
response to identify and build a NameID value, when the response
is processed and consumed.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].name-id-policy-allow-create
docs.description:
Flag to indicate whether the allow-create flags for nameid policies should be set to true, false or ignored/defined. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code TRUE}: Constant to represent the true state.
  • {@code FALSE}: Constant to represent the false state.
  • {@code UNDEFINED}: Constant to represent the undefined state.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].name-id-policy-format
docs.description: NameID policy to request in the authentication requests.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].partial-logout-as-success
docs.description:
Logouts are only successful if the IdP was able to inform all services, otherwise it will
respond with {@code PartialLogout}. This setting allows clients such as CAS to ignore such server-side behavior.
If the IdP reports back a partial logout, this setting instructs CAS whether it should accept or deny that response.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].passive
docs.description: Whether authentication requests should be tagged as passive.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].principal-id-attribute
docs.description:
The attribute found in the identity provider response
that may be used to establish the authenticated
user and build a profile for CAS.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].private-key-password
docs.description: The password to use when generating the private key for the SP/CAS keystore.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].provider-name
docs.description:
Provider name set for the saml authentication request.
Sets the human-readable name of the requester for use by
the presenter's user agent or the identity provider.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].request-initiator-url
docs.description: When generating SAML2 metadata, configure and set the request initiator location attribute.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].requested-attributes
docs.description:
List of attributes requested by the service provider
that would be put into the service provider metadata.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].requested-attributes.friendly-name
docs.description: Attribute friendly name.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].requested-attributes.name
docs.description: Attribute name.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].requested-attributes.name-format
docs.description: Attribute name format.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].requested-attributes.required
docs.description:
Whether this attribute is required and should
be marked so in the metadata.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].response-binding-type
docs.description:
The SAML2 response binding type to use when generating metadata.
This ultimately controls the binding type of the assertion consumer
service in the metadata.
Default value is typically {@code urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST}.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].response-destination-mandatory
docs.description: When validating the response, ensure it has a value set for the {@code Destination} attribute.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].saml2-attribute-converter
docs.description:
Controls the way SAML2 attributes are converted from the authentication response into pac4j attributes.
By default, values of complex types are serialized into a single attribute. To change this behaviour, a
converter class implementing the {@code
AttributeConverter
} interface.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].service-provider-entity-id
docs.description: The entity id of the SP/CAS that is used in the SP metadata generation process.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].sign-authn-request
docs.description: Whether or not the authnRequest should be signed.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].sign-service-provider-logout-request
docs.description: Whether or not the Logout Request sent from the SP should be signed.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].sign-service-provider-metadata
docs.description: Whether or not SAML SP metadata should be signed when generated.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].signature-algorithms
docs.description: Collection of signing signature algorithms, if any, to override the global defaults.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].signature-canonicalization-algorithm
docs.description: The signing signature canonicalization algorithm, if any, to override the global defaults.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].signature-reference-digest-methods
docs.description: Collection of signing signature reference digest methods, if any, to override the global defaults.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].single-logout-service-url
docs.description: When generating SAML2 metadata, configure and set the single logout service URL attribute.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].supported-protocols
docs.description: When generating SAML2 metadata, configure and set the list of supported protocols in the metadata.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].use-name-qualifier
docs.description:
Whether name qualifiers should be produced
in the final saml response.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].wants-assertions-signed
docs.description: Whether metadata should be marked to request sign assertions.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.saml[].wants-responses-signed
docs.description: Whether a response has to be mandatory signed.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.twitter.auto-redirect-type
docs.description:
Auto-redirect to this client. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code SERVER}: Redirect on the server side, typically making CAS invisible.
  • {@code CLIENT}: Redirect on the client side using browser redirects, etc.
  • {@code NONE}: Do nothing and let the selection take place manually.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.twitter.callback-url
docs.description: Callback URL to use to return the flow back to the CAS server one the identity provider is successfully done. This may be used at the discretion of the client and its type to build service parameters, redirect URIs, etc. If none is specified, the CAS server's login endpoint will be used as the basis of the final callback url.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.twitter.callback-url-type
docs.description:
Determine how the callback url should be resolved. Default is {@link CallbackUrlTypes#QUERY_PARAMETER}. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code PATH_PARAMETER}: Path parameter callback url. The client name is added to the path of the callback URL.
  • {@code QUERY_PARAMETER}: Query parameter callback url. The client name is added to the path of a query parameter.
  • {@code NONE}: No callback url. No name is added to the callback URL to be able to distinguish the client.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.twitter.client-name
docs.description: Name of the client mostly for UI purposes and uniqueness. This name, with 'non-word' characters converted to '-' (e.g. "This Org (New)" becomes "This-Org--New-") is added to the "class" attribute of the redirect link on the login page, to allow for custom styling of individual IdPs (e.g. for an organization logo).

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.twitter.css-class
docs.description: CSS class that should be assigned to this client.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.twitter.display-name
docs.description: Indicate the title or display name of the client for decoration and client presentation purposes. If left blank, the client original name would be used by default.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.twitter.enabled
docs.description: Whether the client/external identity provider should be considered active and enabled for integration purposes.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.twitter.id
docs.description: The client id.

docs.name: cas.authn.pac4j.twitter.include-email
docs.description: Set to true to request the user's email address from the Twitter API. For this to have an effect it must first be enabled in the Twitter developer console.

docs.name: cas.authn.password-sync.enabled
docs.description: Allow password synchronization to be turned off globally.

docs.name: cas.authn.password-sync.ldap
docs.description: Options for password sync via LDAP.

docs.name: cas.authn.password-sync.ldap[].allow-multiple-dns
docs.description:
Whether search/query results are allowed to match on multiple DNs,
or whether a single unique DN is expected for the result.

docs.name: cas.authn.password-sync.ldap[].allow-multiple-entries
docs.description: Set if multiple Entries are allowed.

docs.name: cas.authn.password-sync.ldap[].base-dn
docs.description:
Base DN to use.
There may be scenarios where different parts of a single LDAP tree could be considered as base-dns. Rather than duplicating
the LDAP configuration block for each individual base-dn, each entry can be specified
and joined together using a special delimiter character. The user DN is retrieved using the combination of all base-dn and DN
resolvers in the order defined. DN resolution should fail if multiple DNs are found. Otherwise the first DN found is returned.
Usual syntax is: {@code subtreeA,dc=example,dc=net|subtreeC,dc=example,dc=net}.

docs.name: cas.authn.password-sync.ldap[].binary-attributes
docs.description:
Indicate the collection of attributes that are to be tagged and processed as binary
attributes by the underlying search resolver.

docs.name: cas.authn.password-sync.ldap[].bind-credential
docs.description: The bind credential to use when connecting to LDAP.

docs.name: cas.authn.password-sync.ldap[].bind-dn
docs.description:
The bind DN to use when connecting to LDAP. LDAP connection configuration injected into the LDAP connection pool can be initialized with the following parameters:
  • {@code bindDn/bindCredential} provided - Use the provided credentials to bind when initializing connections.
  • {@code bindDn/bindCredential} set to {@code *} - Use a fast-bind strategy to initialize the pool.
  • {@code bindDn/bindCredential} set to blank - Skip connection initializing; perform operations anonymously.
  • SASL mechanism provided - Use the given SASL mechanism to bind when initializing connections.

docs.name: cas.authn.password-sync.ldap[].block-wait-time
docs.description:
The length of time the pool will block.
By default the pool will block indefinitely and there is no guarantee that

docs.name: cas.authn.password-sync.ldap[].pool-passivator
docs.description:
You may receive unexpected LDAP failures, when CAS is configured to authenticate using {@code DIRECT} or {@code AUTHENTICATED} types and LDAP is locked down to not allow anonymous binds/searches. Every second attempt with a given LDAP connection from the pool would fail if it was on the same connection as a failed login attempt, and the regular connection validator would similarly fail. When a connection is returned back to a pool, it still may contain the principal and credentials from the previous attempt. Before the next bind attempt using that connection, the validator tries to validate the connection again but fails because it’s no longer trying with the configured bind credentials but with whatever user DN was used in the previous step. Given the validation failure, the connection is closed and CAS would deny access by default. Passivators attempt to reconnect to LDAP with the configured bind credentials, effectively resetting the connection to what it should be after each bind request. Furthermore if you are seeing errors in the logs that resemble a 'Operation exception encountered, reopening connection' type of message, this usually is an indication that the connection pool’s validation timeout established and created by CAS is greater than the timeout configured in the LDAP server, or more likely, in the load balancer in front of the LDAP servers. You can adjust the LDAP server session’s timeout for connections, or you can teach CAS to use a validity period that is equal or less than the LDAP server session’s timeout. Accepted values are:
  • {@code NONE}: No passivation takes place.
  • {@code BIND}: The default behavior which passivates a connection by performing a bind operation on it. This option requires the availability of bind credentials when establishing connections to LDAP.

docs.name: cas.authn.password-sync.ldap[].search-entry-handlers.type
docs.description:
The type of search entry handler to choose. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code FOLLOW_SEARCH_REFERRAL}: Provides handling of an ldap referral for search operations.
  • {@code FOLLOW_SEARCH_RESULT_REFERENCE}: Provides handling of an ldap continuation reference for search operations.
  • {@code ACTIVE_DIRECTORY}: Process the entry results fetched from active directory and check for account status controls for disabled/expired accounts, etc.
  • {@code OBJECT_GUID}: Object guid search entry handler. Handles the {@code objectGUID} attribute fetching and conversion.
  • {@code OBJECT_SID}: Object sid search entry handler. Handles the {@code objectSid} attribute fetching and conversion.
  • {@code CASE_CHANGE}: Case change search entry handler. Provides the ability to modify the case of search entry DNs, attribute names, and attribute values.
  • {@code DN_ATTRIBUTE_ENTRY}: DN attribute entry handler. Adds the entry DN as an attribute to the result set. Provides a client side implementation of RFC 5020.
  • {@code MERGE}: Merge search entry handler. Merges the values of one or more attributes into a single attribute.
  • {@code PRIMARY_GROUP}: Primary group search handler. Constructs the primary group SID and then searches for that group and puts it's DN in the {@code memberOf} attribute of the original search entry.
  • {@code RANGE_ENTRY}: Range entry search handler. Rewrites attributes returned from Active Directory to include all values by performing additional searches.
  • {@code RECURSIVE_ENTRY}: Recursive entry search handler. This recursively searches based on a supplied attribute and merges those results into the original entry.
  • {@code MERGE_ENTRIES}: Merge entries handler. Merges the values of one or more attributes in all entries into a single attribute. The merged attribute may or may not already exist on the entry. If it does exist it's existing values will remain intact.

docs.name: cas.authn.passwordless.accounts.ldap.search-entry-handlers[].type
docs.description:
The type of search entry handler to choose. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code FOLLOW_SEARCH_REFERRAL}: Provides handling of an ldap referral for search operations.
  • {@code FOLLOW_SEARCH_RESULT_REFERENCE}: Provides handling of an ldap continuation reference for search operations.
  • {@code ACTIVE_DIRECTORY}: Process the entry results fetched from active directory and check for account status controls for disabled/expired accounts, etc.
  • {@code OBJECT_GUID}: Object guid search entry handler. Handles the {@code objectGUID} attribute fetching and conversion.
  • {@code OBJECT_SID}: Object sid search entry handler. Handles the {@code objectSid} attribute fetching and conversion.
  • {@code CASE_CHANGE}: Case change search entry handler. Provides the ability to modify the case of search entry DNs, attribute names, and attribute values.
  • {@code DN_ATTRIBUTE_ENTRY}: DN attribute entry handler. Adds the entry DN as an attribute to the result set. Provides a client side implementation of RFC 5020.
  • {@code MERGE}: Merge search entry handler. Merges the values of one or more attributes into a single attribute.
  • {@code PRIMARY_GROUP}: Primary group search handler. Constructs the primary group SID and then searches for that group and puts it's DN in the {@code memberOf} attribute of the original search entry.
  • {@code RANGE_ENTRY}: Range entry search handler. Rewrites attributes returned from Active Directory to include all values by performing additional searches.
  • {@code RECURSIVE_ENTRY}: Recursive entry search handler. This recursively searches based on a supplied attribute and merges those results into the original entry.
  • {@code MERGE_ENTRIES}: Merge entries handler. Merges the values of one or more attributes in all entries into a single attribute. The merged attribute may or may not already exist on the entry. If it does exist it's existing values will remain intact.

docs.name: cas.authn.passwordless.core.delegated-authentication-selector-script.location
docs.description:
The location of the resource. Resources can be URLs, or files found either on the classpath or outside somewhere in the file system.

In the event the configured resource is a Groovy script, especially if the script is set to reload on changes, you may need to adjust the total number of {@code inotify} instances. On Linux, you may need to add the following line to {@code /etc/sysctl.conf}: {@code fs.inotify.max_user_instances = 256}.

You can check the current value via {@code cat /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances}.

In situations and scenarios where CAS is able to automatically watch the underlying resource for changes and detect updates and modifications dynamically, you may be able to specify the following setting as either an environment variable or system property with a value of {@code false} to disable the resource watcher: {@code org.apereo.cas.util.io.PathWatcherService}.

docs.name: cas.authn.passwordless.core.multifactor-authentication-activated
docs.description:
Allow passwordless authentication to skip its own flow in favor of multifactor authentication providers that may be available and defined in CAS.

If multifactor authentication is activated, and defined MFA triggers in CAS signal availability and eligibility of an MFA flow for the given passwordless user, CAS will skip its normal passwordless authentication flow in favor of the requested multifactor authentication provider. If no MFA providers are available, or if no triggers require MFA for the verified passwordless user, passwordless authentication flow will commence as usual.

docs.name: cas.authn.passwordless.google-recaptcha.score
docs.description: Google reCAPTCHA v3 returns a score (1.0 is very likely a good interaction, 0.0 is very likely a bot). reCAPTCHA learns by seeing real traffic on your site. For this reason, scores in a staging environment or soon after implementing may differ from production. As reCAPTCHA v3 doesn't ever interrupt the user flow, you can first run reCAPTCHA without taking action and then decide on thresholds by looking at your traffic in the admin console. By default, you can use a threshold of 0.5.

  • For Google reCAPTCHA, the endpoint is {@code https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify}.
  • For hCaptcha, the endpoint is {@code https://hcaptcha.com/siteverify}.
  • For Turnstile, the endpoint is {@code https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify}.

docs.name: cas.authn.passwordless.google-recaptcha.version
docs.description:
Indicate the version of the recaptcha api. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA_V2}: V2 version of the recaptcha API.
  • {@code GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA_V3}: V3 version of the recaptcha API.
  • {@code HCAPTCHA}: hCaptcha is an alternative to reCAPTCHA that requires website visitors to label images as part of its business model. The provider is more focused on manual image recognition challenges. It is a image classification task based CAPTCHA provider employing visual challenges like identifying objects.
  • {@code TURNSTILE}: Offers a CAPTCHA alternative by Cloudflare that prioritizes user experience and privacy. Turnstile delivers frustration-free, CAPTCHA-free web experiences to website visitors - with just a simple snippet of free code. Moreover, Turnstile stops abuse and confirms visitors are real without the data privacy concerns or awful user experience of CAPTCHAs.
  • {@code FRIENDLY_CAPTCHA}: Friendly captcha is a European alternative, accessible and GDPR compliant.

docs.name: cas.authn.passwordless.tokens.jpa.ddl-auto
docs.description:
Hibernate feature to automatically validate and exports DDL to the schema. By default, creates and drops the schema automatically when a session is starts and ends. Setting the value to {@code validate} or {@code none} may be more desirable for production, but any of the following options can be used:
  • {@code validate}: Validate the schema, but make no changes to the database.
  • {@code update}: Update the schema.
  • {@code create}: Create the schema, destroying previous data.
  • {@code create-drop}: Drop the schema at the end of the session.
  • {@code none}: Do nothing.

Note that during a version migration where any schema has changed {@code create-drop} will result in the loss of all data as soon as CAS is started. For transient data like tickets this is probably not an issue, but in cases like the audit table important data could be lost. Using `update`, while safe for data, is confirmed to result in invalid database state. {@code validate} or {@code none} settings are likely the only safe options for production use.

For more info, see this.

docs.name: cas.authn.passwordless.tokens.jpa.fail-fast-timeout
docs.description:
Set the pool initialization failure timeout.
  • Any value greater than zero will be treated as a timeout for pool initialization. The calling thread will be blocked from continuing until a successful connection to the database, or until the timeout is reached. If the timeout is reached, then a {@code PoolInitializationException} will be thrown.
  • A value of zero will not prevent the pool from starting in the case that a connection cannot be obtained. However, upon start the pool will attempt to obtain a connection and validate that the {@code connectionTestQuery} and {@code connectionInitSql} are valid. If those validations fail, an exception will be thrown. If a connection cannot be obtained, the validation is skipped and the pool will start and continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
  • A value less than zero will not bypass any connection attempt and validation during startup, and therefore the pool will start immediately. The pool will continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
Note that if this timeout value is greater than or equal to zero (0), and therefore an initial connection validation is performed, this timeout does not override the {@code connectionTimeout} or {@code validationTimeout}; they will be honored before this timeout is applied. The default value is one millisecond.

docs.name: cas.authn.pm.forgot-username.google-recaptcha.version
docs.description:
Indicate the version of the recaptcha api. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA_V2}: V2 version of the recaptcha API.
  • {@code GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA_V3}: V3 version of the recaptcha API.
  • {@code HCAPTCHA}: hCaptcha is an alternative to reCAPTCHA that requires website visitors to label images as part of its business model. The provider is more focused on manual image recognition challenges. It is a image classification task based CAPTCHA provider employing visual challenges like identifying objects.
  • {@code TURNSTILE}: Offers a CAPTCHA alternative by Cloudflare that prioritizes user experience and privacy. Turnstile delivers frustration-free, CAPTCHA-free web experiences to website visitors - with just a simple snippet of free code. Moreover, Turnstile stops abuse and confirms visitors are real without the data privacy concerns or awful user experience of CAPTCHAs.
  • {@code FRIENDLY_CAPTCHA}: Friendly captcha is a European alternative, accessible and GDPR compliant.

docs.name: cas.authn.pm.groovy.location
docs.description:
The location of the resource. Resources can be URLs, or files found either on the classpath or outside somewhere in the file system.

In the event the configured resource is a Groovy script, especially if the script is set to reload on changes, you may need to adjust the total number of {@code inotify} instances. On Linux, you may need to add the following line to {@code /etc/sysctl.conf}: {@code fs.inotify.max_user_instances = 256}.

You can check the current value via {@code cat /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances}.

In situations and scenarios where CAS is able to automatically watch the underlying resource for changes and detect updates and modifications dynamically, you may be able to specify the following setting as either an environment variable or system property with a value of {@code false} to disable the resource watcher: {@code org.apereo.cas.util.io.PathWatcherService}.

docs.name: cas.authn.pm.jdbc.ddl-auto
docs.description:
Hibernate feature to automatically validate and exports DDL to the schema. By default, creates and drops the schema automatically when a session is starts and ends. Setting the value to {@code validate} or {@code none} may be more desirable for production, but any of the following options can be used:
  • {@code validate}: Validate the schema, but make no changes to the database.
  • {@code update}: Update the schema.
  • {@code create}: Create the schema, destroying previous data.
  • {@code create-drop}: Drop the schema at the end of the session.
  • {@code none}: Do nothing.

Note that during a version migration where any schema has changed {@code create-drop} will result in the loss of all data as soon as CAS is started. For transient data like tickets this is probably not an issue, but in cases like the audit table important data could be lost. Using `update`, while safe for data, is confirmed to result in invalid database state. {@code validate} or {@code none} settings are likely the only safe options for production use.

For more info, see this.

docs.name: cas.authn.pm.jdbc.dialect

docs.name: cas.authn.pm.jdbc.driver-class

docs.name: cas.authn.pm.jdbc.fail-fast-timeout
docs.description:
Set the pool initialization failure timeout.
  • Any value greater than zero will be treated as a timeout for pool initialization. The calling thread will be blocked from continuing until a successful connection to the database, or until the timeout is reached. If the timeout is reached, then a {@code PoolInitializationException} will be thrown.
  • A value of zero will not prevent the pool from starting in the case that a connection cannot be obtained. However, upon start the pool will attempt to obtain a connection and validate that the {@code connectionTestQuery} and {@code connectionInitSql} are valid. If those validations fail, an exception will be thrown. If a connection cannot be obtained, the validation is skipped and the pool will start and continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
  • A value less than zero will not bypass any connection attempt and validation during startup, and therefore the pool will start immediately. The pool will continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
Note that if this timeout value is greater than or equal to zero (0), and therefore an initial connection validation is performed, this timeout does not override the {@code connectionTimeout} or {@code validationTimeout}; they will be honored before this timeout is applied. The default value is one millisecond.

Since these are typically read-only queries, it is rarely necessary to encapsulate them in their own transaction. This property only applies if {@link #autocommit} is disabled.

docs.name: cas.authn.pm.jdbc.password-encoder.strength
docs.description: Strength or number of iterations to use for password hashing. Usually relevant when dealing with {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#BCRYPT}, {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#PBKDF2} or {@link PasswordEncoderTypes#GLIBC_CRYPT}. docs.name: cas.authn.pm.jdbc.password-encoder.type
docs.description:
Define the password encoder type to use. Type may be specified as blank or {@code NONE} to disable password encoding. It may also refer to a fully-qualified class name that implements the Spring Security's {@code PasswordEncoder} interface if you wish you define your own encoder.

The following types may be used:

  • {@code NONE}: No password encoding (i.e. plain-text) takes place.
  • {@code DEFAULT}: Use the {@code DefaultPasswordEncoder} of CAS. For message-digest algorithms via {@code character-encoding} and {@code encoding-algorithm}.
  • {@code BCRYPT}: Use the {@code BCryptPasswordEncoder} based on the strength provided and an optional secret.
  • {@code SCRYPT}: Use the {@code SCryptPasswordEncoder}.
  • {@code PBKDF2}: Use the {@code Pbkdf2PasswordEncoder} based on the strength provided and an optional secret.
  • {@code STANDARD}: Use the {@code StandardPasswordEncoder} based on the secret provided.
  • {@code SSHA}: Use the {@code LdapShaPasswordEncoder} supports Ldap SHA and SSHA (salted-SHA). The values are base-64 encoded and have the label {SHA} or {SSHA} prepended to the encoded hash.
  • {@code GLIBC_CRYPT}: Use the {@code GlibcCryptPasswordEncoder} based on the {@code encoding-algorithm}, strength provided and an optional secret.
  • {@code org.example.MyEncoder}: An implementation of {@code PasswordEncoder} of your own choosing.
  • {@code file:///path/to/script.groovy}: Path to a Groovy script charged with handling password encoding operations.

For Active Directory and in scenarios where {@link #accountLockedAttribute} is set to {@code lockoutTime}, this value might be set to zero. A value of zero means that the account is not currently locked out.

docs.name: cas.authn.pm.ldap[].base-dn
docs.description:
Base DN to use.
There may be scenarios where different parts of a single LDAP tree could be considered as base-dns. Rather than duplicating
the LDAP configuration block for each individual base-dn, each entry can be specified
and joined together using a special delimiter character. The user DN is retrieved using the combination of all base-dn and DN
resolvers in the order defined. DN resolution should fail if multiple DNs are found. Otherwise the first DN found is returned.
Usual syntax is: {@code subtreeA,dc=example,dc=net|subtreeC,dc=example,dc=net}.

  • {@code bindDn/bindCredential} provided - Use the provided credentials to bind when initializing connections.
  • {@code bindDn/bindCredential} set to {@code *} - Use a fast-bind strategy to initialize the pool.
  • {@code bindDn/bindCredential} set to blank - Skip connection initializing; perform operations anonymously.
  • SASL mechanism provided - Use the given SASL mechanism to bind when initializing connections.

By default the pool will block indefinitely and there is no guarantee that

number of connections that can be created

  • {@code ROUND_ROBIN} For each new connection the next url in the list will be used.
  • {@code RANDOM} For each new connection a random LDAP url will be selected.
  • {@code DNS_SRV} LDAP urls based on DNS SRV records of the configured/given LDAP url will be used.

docs.name: cas.authn.pm.ldap[].pool-passivator
docs.description:
You may receive unexpected LDAP failures, when CAS is configured to authenticate using {@code DIRECT} or {@code AUTHENTICATED} types and LDAP is locked down to not allow anonymous binds/searches. Every second attempt with a given LDAP connection from the pool would fail if it was on the same connection as a failed login attempt, and the regular connection validator would similarly fail. When a connection is returned back to a pool, it still may contain the principal and credentials from the previous attempt. Before the next bind attempt using that connection, the validator tries to validate the connection again but fails because it’s no longer trying with the configured bind credentials but with whatever user DN was used in the previous step. Given the validation failure, the connection is closed and CAS would deny access by default. Passivators attempt to reconnect to LDAP with the configured bind credentials, effectively resetting the connection to what it should be after each bind request. Furthermore if you are seeing errors in the logs that resemble a 'Operation exception encountered, reopening connection' type of message, this usually is an indication that the connection pool’s validation timeout established and created by CAS is greater than the timeout configured in the LDAP server, or more likely, in the load balancer in front of the LDAP servers. You can adjust the LDAP server session’s timeout for connections, or you can teach CAS to use a validity period that is equal or less than the LDAP server session’s timeout. Accepted values are:
  • {@code NONE}: No passivation takes place.
  • {@code BIND}: The default behavior which passivates a connection by performing a bind operation on it. This option requires the availability of bind credentials when establishing connections to LDAP.

You can check the current value via {@code cat /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances}.

In situations and scenarios where CAS is able to automatically watch the underlying resource for changes and detect updates and modifications dynamically, you may be able to specify the following setting as either an environment variable or system property with a value of {@code false} to disable the resource watcher: {@code org.apereo.cas.util.io.PathWatcherService}.

docs.name: cas.authn.pm.ldap[].search-entry-handlers.type
docs.description:
The type of search entry handler to choose. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code FOLLOW_SEARCH_REFERRAL}: Provides handling of an ldap referral for search operations.
  • {@code FOLLOW_SEARCH_RESULT_REFERENCE}: Provides handling of an ldap continuation reference for search operations.
  • {@code ACTIVE_DIRECTORY}: Process the entry results fetched from active directory and check for account status controls for disabled/expired accounts, etc.
  • {@code OBJECT_GUID}: Object guid search entry handler. Handles the {@code objectGUID} attribute fetching and conversion.
  • {@code OBJECT_SID}: Object sid search entry handler. Handles the {@code objectSid} attribute fetching and conversion.
  • {@code CASE_CHANGE}: Case change search entry handler. Provides the ability to modify the case of search entry DNs, attribute names, and attribute values.
  • {@code DN_ATTRIBUTE_ENTRY}: DN attribute entry handler. Adds the entry DN as an attribute to the result set. Provides a client side implementation of RFC 5020.
  • {@code MERGE}: Merge search entry handler. Merges the values of one or more attributes into a single attribute.
  • {@code PRIMARY_GROUP}: Primary group search handler. Constructs the primary group SID and then searches for that group and puts it's DN in the {@code memberOf} attribute of the original search entry.
  • {@code RANGE_ENTRY}: Range entry search handler. Rewrites attributes returned from Active Directory to include all values by performing additional searches.
  • {@code RECURSIVE_ENTRY}: Recursive entry search handler. This recursively searches based on a supplied attribute and merges those results into the original entry.
  • {@code MERGE_ENTRIES}: Merge entries handler. Merges the values of one or more attributes in all entries into a single attribute. The merged attribute may or may not already exist on the entry. If it does exist it's existing values will remain intact.

docs.name: cas.authn.pm.reset.confirmation-mail.priority
docs.description: Set the priority ({@code X-Priority} header) of the message. Values: {@code 1 (Highest)}, {@code 2 (High)}, {@code 3 (Normal)}, {@code 4 (Low)}, {@code 5 (Lowest)}. The application of this setting depends on the email provider implementation and may not be fully supported everywhere. This is typically relevant for the default {@link org.springframework.mail.javamail.JavaMailSender}.

docs.name: cas.authn.pm.reset.confirmation-mail.subject
docs.description:
Email subject line.

The subject can either be defined verbatim, or it may point to a message key in the language bundle using the syntax {@code #{subject-language-key}}. This key should point to a valid message defined in the appropriate language bundle that is then picked up via the active locale. In case where the language code cannot resolve the real subject, a default subject value would be used.

docs.name: cas.authn.pm.reset.confirmation-mail.text
docs.description:
Email message body. Could be plain text or a reference to an external file that would serve as a template.

If specified as a path to an external file with an extension {@code .gtemplate}, then the email message body would be processed using the Groovy template engine. The template engine uses JSP style <% %> script and <%= %> expression syntax or GString style expressions. The variable {@code out} is bound to the writer that the template is being written to.

If using plain text, the contents are processed for string substitution candidates using named variables. For example, you may refer to an expected url variable in the email text via {@code ${url}}, or use {@code ${token}} to locate the token variable. In certain cases, additional parameters are passed to the email body processor that might include authentication and/or principal attributes, the available locale, client http information, etc.

docs.name: cas.authn.pm.reset.confirmation-mail.validate-addresses

If specified as a path to an external file with an extension {@code .gtemplate}, then the email message body would be processed using the Groovy template engine. The template engine uses JSP style <% %> script and <%= %> expression syntax or GString style expressions. The variable {@code out} is bound to the writer that the template is being written to.

If using plain text, the contents are processed for string substitution candidates using named variables. For example, you may refer to an expected url variable in the email text via {@code ${url}}, or use {@code ${token}} to locate the token variable. In certain cases, additional parameters are passed to the email body processor that might include authentication and/or principal attributes, the available locale, client http information, etc.

docs.description:
Configure allowed {@code Origin} header values. This check is mostly designed for browser clients. There is nothing preventing other types of client to modify the {@code Origin} header value.

When SockJS is enabled and origins are restricted, transport types that do not allow to check request origin (Iframe based transports) are disabled. As a consequence, IE 6 to 9 are not supported when origins are restricted.

Each provided allowed origin must start by "http://", "https://" or be "*" (means that all origins are allowed). By default, only same origin requests are allowed (empty list).

In the event the configured resource is a Groovy script, especially if the script is set to reload on changes, you may need to adjust the total number of {@code inotify} instances. On Linux, you may need to add the following line to {@code /etc/sysctl.conf}: {@code fs.inotify.max_user_instances = 256}.

You can check the current value via {@code cat /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances}.

In situations and scenarios where CAS is able to automatically watch the underlying resource for changes and detect updates and modifications dynamically, you may be able to specify the following setting as either an environment variable or system property with a value of {@code false} to disable the resource watcher: {@code org.apereo.cas.util.io.PathWatcherService}.

docs.name: cas.authn.radius.password-encoder.type
docs.description:
Define the password encoder type to use. Type may be specified as blank or {@code NONE} to disable password encoding. It may also refer to a fully-qualified class name that implements the Spring Security's {@code PasswordEncoder} interface if you wish you define your own encoder.

The following types may be used:

  • {@code NONE}: No password encoding (i.e. plain-text) takes place.
  • {@code DEFAULT}: Use the {@code DefaultPasswordEncoder} of CAS. For message-digest algorithms via {@code character-encoding} and {@code encoding-algorithm}.
  • {@code BCRYPT}: Use the {@code BCryptPasswordEncoder} based on the strength provided and an optional secret.
  • {@code SCRYPT}: Use the {@code SCryptPasswordEncoder}.
  • {@code PBKDF2}: Use the {@code Pbkdf2PasswordEncoder} based on the strength provided and an optional secret.
  • {@code STANDARD}: Use the {@code StandardPasswordEncoder} based on the secret provided.
  • {@code SSHA}: Use the {@code LdapShaPasswordEncoder} supports Ldap SHA and SSHA (salted-SHA). The values are base-64 encoded and have the label {SHA} or {SSHA} prepended to the encoded hash.
  • {@code GLIBC_CRYPT}: Use the {@code GlibcCryptPasswordEncoder} based on the {@code encoding-algorithm}, strength provided and an optional secret.
  • {@code org.example.MyEncoder}: An implementation of {@code PasswordEncoder} of your own choosing.
  • {@code file:///path/to/script.groovy}: Path to a Groovy script charged with handling password encoding operations.

docs.name: cas.authn.redis.pool.enabled
docs.description: Enable the pooling configuration.

docs.name: cas.authn.redis.pool.fairness
docs.description: Returns whether or not the pool serves threads waiting to borrow objects fairly. True means that waiting threads are served as if waiting in a FIFO queue.

docs.name: cas.authn.redis.pool.lifo
docs.description: Returns whether the pool has LIFO (last in, first out) behaviour with respect to idle objects - always returning the most recently used object from the pool, or as a FIFO (first in, first out) queue, where the pool always returns the oldest object in the idle object pool.

docs.name: cas.authn.redis.pool.max-active
docs.description: Max number of connections that can be allocated by the pool at a given time. Use a negative value for no limit.

docs.name: cas.authn.redis.pool.max-idle
docs.description: Max number of "idle" connections in the pool. Use a negative value to indicate an unlimited number of idle connections.

docs.name: cas.authn.redis.pool.max-wait
docs.description: Maximum amount of time (in milliseconds) a connection allocation should block before throwing an exception when the pool is exhausted. Use a negative value to block indefinitely.

docs.name: cas.authn.redis.pool.min-evictable-idle-time-millis
docs.description: Sets the minimum amount of time an object may sit idle in the pool before it is eligible for eviction by the idle object evictor (if any - see setTimeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis(long)). When non-positive, no objects will be evicted from the pool due to idle time alone.

docs.name: cas.authn.redis.pool.min-idle
docs.description: Target for the minimum number of idle connections to maintain in the pool. This setting only has an effect if it is positive.

docs.name: cas.authn.redis.pool.num-tests-per-eviction-run
docs.description: Sets the maximum number of objects to examine during each run (if any) of the idle object evictor thread. When positive, the number of tests performed for a run will be the minimum of the configured value and the number of idle instances in the pool. When negative, the number of tests performed will be ceil(getNumIdle()/ abs(getNumTestsPerEvictionRun())) which means that when the value is -n roughly one nth of the idle objects will be tested per run.

docs.name: cas.authn.redis.pool.soft-min-evictable-idle-time-millis
docs.description: Sets the minimum amount of time an object may sit idle in the pool before it is eligible for eviction by the idle object evictor (if any - see setTimeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis(long)), with the extra condition that at least minIdle object instances remain in the pool. This setting is overridden by getMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() (that is, if getMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() is positive, then getSoftMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() is ignored).

docs.name: cas.authn.redis.pool.test-on-borrow
docs.description: Returns whether objects borrowed from the pool will be validated before being returned from the borrowObject() method. Validation is performed by the validateObject() method of the factory associated with the pool. If the object fails to validate, it will be removed from the pool and destroyed, and a new attempt will be made to borrow an object from the pool.

docs.name: cas.authn.redis.pool.test-on-create
docs.description: Returns whether objects created for the pool will be validated before being returned from the borrowObject() method. Validation is performed by the validateObject() method of the factory associated with the pool. If the object fails to validate, then borrowObject() will fail.

docs.name: cas.authn.redis.pool.test-on-return
docs.description: Returns whether objects borrowed from the pool will be validated when they are returned to the pool via the returnObject() method. Validation is performed by the validateObject() method of the factory associated with the pool. Returning objects that fail validation are destroyed rather then being returned the pool.

docs.name: cas.authn.redis.pool.test-while-idle
docs.description: Returns whether objects sitting idle in the pool will be validated by the idle object evictor ( if any - see setTimeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis(long)). Validation is performed by the validateObject() method of the factory associated with the pool. If the object fails to validate, it will be removed from the pool and destroyed.

docs.name: cas.authn.redis.pool.time-between-eviction-runs-millis
docs.description: Sets the amount of time (in milliseconds) between runs of the idle object evictor thread. When non-positive, no idle object evictor thread will be run. If positive, the idle object evictor thread will run at least once every timeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis milliseconds, and will attempt to evict objects from the pool that are idle longer than getMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() (if positive) or getSoftMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() (if positive).

In the event the configured resource is a Groovy script, especially if the script is set to reload on changes, you may need to adjust the total number of {@code inotify} instances. On Linux, you may need to add the following line to {@code /etc/sysctl.conf}: {@code fs.inotify.max_user_instances = 256}.

You can check the current value via {@code cat /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances}.

In situations and scenarios where CAS is able to automatically watch the underlying resource for changes and detect updates and modifications dynamically, you may be able to specify the following setting as either an environment variable or system property with a value of {@code false} to disable the resource watcher: {@code org.apereo.cas.util.io.PathWatcherService}.

docs.name: cas.authn.redis.read-from
docs.description:
Setting that describes how Lettuce routes read operations to replica nodes. Note that modes referencing MASTER/SLAVE are deprecated (but still supported) in the Lettuce redis client dependency so migrate config to UPSTREAM/REPLICA. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code UPSTREAM}: Read from the current upstream node.
  • {@code UPSTREAMPREFERRED}: Read from the upstream node, but if it is unavailable, read from replica nodes.
  • {@code MASTER}: Read from the current upstream node.
  • {@code MASTERPREFERRED}: Read from the upstream node, but if it is unavailable, read from replica nodes.
  • {@code SLAVE}: Read from replica nodes.
  • {@code SLAVEPREFERRED}: Read from the replica nodes, but if none is unavailable, read from the upstream node.
  • {@code REPLICA}: Read from replica nodes.
  • {@code REPLICAPREFERRED}: Read from the replica nodes, but if none is unavailable, read from the upstream node.
  • {@code ANY}: Read from any node of the cluster.
  • {@code ANYREPLICA}: Read from any replica node of the cluster.
  • {@code NEAREST}: Read from the nearest node.

docs.name: cas.authn.redis.scan-count
docs.description: Redis scan count option. When and if specified, SCAN operations would be "counted" or limited by this setting. While SCAN does not provide guarantees about the number of elements returned at every iteration, it is possible to empirically adjust the behavior of SCAN using the COUNT option. Basically with COUNT the user specified the amount of work that should be done at every call in order to retrieve elements from the collection. This is just a hint for the implementation, however generally speaking this is what you could expect most of the times from the implementation.

docs.name: cas.authn.redis.share-native-connections
docs.description: The shared native connection is never closed by Lettuce connection, therefore it is not validated by default when connections are retrieved. If this setting is {@code true}, a shared connection will be used for regular operations and a connection provider will be used to select a connection for blocking and tx operations only, which should not share a connection. If native connection sharing is disabled, new (or pooled) connections will be used for all operations. By default, multiple connections share a single thread-safe native connection. If you enable connection pooling, then native connection sharing will be disabled and the connection pool will be used for all operations. You may however explicitly control connection sharing via this setting as an override.

  • {@code org.example.MyEncoder}: An implementation of {@code PasswordEncoder} of your own choosing.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.core.context.authentication-context-class-mappings
docs.description:
A mapping of authentication context class refs. This is where specific authentication context classes are referenced and mapped to providers that CAS may support mainly for, i.e. MFA purposes.

Example might be {@code urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:SomeClassName->mfa-duo}.

In delegated authentication scenarios, this can also be a mapping of authentication context class refs, when CAS is proxying/delegating authentication to an external SAML2 identity provider. The requested authentication context as submitted by the service provider is first received by CAS, and then gets mapped to a context class that is passed onto the external identity provider. For example, you might have a scenario where a SAML2 service provider would submit {@code https://refeds.org/profile/mfa} to CAS, and CAS would translate that to {@code http://schemas.microsoft.com/claims/multipleauthn} to ultimate route the authentication request to Azure. If no mapping is found, the original context is passed as is.

Example might be {@code https://refeds.org/profile/mfa->http://schemas.microsoft.com/claims/multipleauthn}.

A negative value means that the cookie is not stored persistently and will be deleted when the Web browser exits. A zero value causes the cookie to be deleted.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.core.session-replication.cookie.name
docs.description: Cookie name. Constructs a cookie with a specified name and value. The name must conform to RFC 2965. That means it can contain only ASCII alphanumeric characters and cannot contain commas, semicolons, or white space or begin with a {@code $} character. The cookie's name cannot be changed after creation. By default, cookies are created according to the RFC 2965 cookie specification. Cookie names are automatically calculated assigned by CAS at runtime, and there is usually no need to customize the name or assign it a different value unless a special use case warrants the change.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.core.session-replication.cookie.path
docs.description: Cookie path. Specifies a path for the cookie to which the client should return the cookie. The cookie is visible to all the pages in the directory you specify, and all the pages in that directory's subdirectories. A cookie's path must include the servlet that set the cookie, for example, /catalog, which makes the cookie visible to all directories on the server under /catalog. Consult RFC 2965 (available on the Internet) for more information on setting path names for cookies.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.core.session-replication.cookie.pin-to-session
docs.description:
When generating cookie values, determine whether the value should be compounded and signed with the properties of the current session, such as IP address, user-agent, etc.

Turning off session pinning is not exactly ideal. This is a barrier to prevent cookie replay attacks. A cookie that was created with an IP given a certain location cannot be replayed back in a different browser with a different IP from a different location.

There may however be legitimate reasons to turn it off and relax this after careful reviews, if you intend to support a type of user who intends to switch their IP quite frequently. A classic example is the type of user that is on VPN at the time of login, but decides to resume their work a few hours later off VPN or at a different location.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.core.session-replication.cookie.same-site-policy
docs.description:
If a cookie is only intended to be accessed in a first party context, the developer has the option to apply one of settings {@code SameSite=Lax} or {@code SameSite=Strict} or {@code SameSite=None} to prevent external access.

To safeguard more websites and their users, the new secure-by-default model assumes all cookies should be protected from external access unless otherwise specified. Developers must use a new cookie setting, {@code SameSite=None}, to designate cookies for cross-site access. When the {@code SameSite=None} attribute is present, an additional {@code Secure} attribute is used so cross-site cookies can only be accessed over HTTPS connections.

Accepted values are:
  • {@code Lax}
  • {@code Strict}
  • {@code None}
  • {@code Off}: Disable the generation of the SameSite cookie attribute altogether.
  • Path to a Groovy script that is able to generate the SameSite cookie attribute dynamically.
  • Fully qualified name of a class that implements {@code org.apereo.cas.web.cookie.CookieSameSitePolicy}

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.core.session-storage-type
docs.description:
Indicates whether saml requests, and other session data, collected as part of SAML flows and requests that are kept by the container http session, local storage, or should be replicated across the cluster. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code HTTP}: Authentication requests, and other session data collected as part of authentication protocol flows and requests are kept in the http servlet session that is local to the server.
  • {@code BROWSER_STORAGE}: Authentication requests, and other session data collected as part of authentication protocol flows and requests are kept in the client browser's session storage, signed and encrypted. All interactions require client-side read/write operations to restore the session from the browser.
  • {@code TICKET_REGISTRY}: Authentication requests, and other session data collected as part of authentication protocol flows and requests are tracked as CAS tickets in the registry and replicated across the entire cluster as tickets. This state is tied to the user's agent/browser using a special cookie that would be used to locate and restore that state. The cookie content may be signed and encrypted.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.metadata.dynamo-db.billing-mode
docs.description:
Billing mode specifies how you are charged for read and write throughput and how you manage capacity. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code PROVISIONED}: Provisioned mode means that you specify the number of reads and writes per second that you expect your application to use. Provisioned mode is a good option if any of the following are true:
    • You have predictable application traffic.
    • You run applications whose traffic is consistent or ramps gradually.
    • You can forecast capacity requirements to control costs.
    You can use auto scaling to automatically adjust capacity based on the specified utilization rate to ensure application performance while reducing costs.
  • {@code PAY_PER_REQUEST}: Pay-per-request or on-demand billing means that you're charged for only the read/write requests that you use. On-demand mode is a good option if any of the following are true:
    • You create new tables with unknown workloads.
    • You have unpredictable application traffic.
    • You prefer the ease of paying for only what you use.
    Tables using on-demand mode support all DynamoDB features (such as encryption at rest, point-in-time recovery, global tables, and so on) with the exception of auto scaling, which is not applicable with this mode.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.metadata.jpa.ddl-auto
docs.description:
Hibernate feature to automatically validate and exports DDL to the schema. By default, creates and drops the schema automatically when a session is starts and ends. Setting the value to {@code validate} or {@code none} may be more desirable for production, but any of the following options can be used:
  • {@code validate}: Validate the schema, but make no changes to the database.
  • {@code update}: Update the schema.
  • {@code create}: Create the schema, destroying previous data.
  • {@code create-drop}: Drop the schema at the end of the session.
  • {@code none}: Do nothing.

Note that during a version migration where any schema has changed {@code create-drop} will result in the loss of all data as soon as CAS is started. For transient data like tickets this is probably not an issue, but in cases like the audit table important data could be lost. Using `update`, while safe for data, is confirmed to result in invalid database state. {@code validate} or {@code none} settings are likely the only safe options for production use.

For more info, see this.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.metadata.jpa.fail-fast-timeout
docs.description:
Set the pool initialization failure timeout.
  • Any value greater than zero will be treated as a timeout for pool initialization. The calling thread will be blocked from continuing until a successful connection to the database, or until the timeout is reached. If the timeout is reached, then a {@code PoolInitializationException} will be thrown.
  • A value of zero will not prevent the pool from starting in the case that a connection cannot be obtained. However, upon start the pool will attempt to obtain a connection and validate that the {@code connectionTestQuery} and {@code connectionInitSql} are valid. If those validations fail, an exception will be thrown. If a connection cannot be obtained, the validation is skipped and the pool will start and continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
  • A value less than zero will not bypass any connection attempt and validation during startup, and therefore the pool will start immediately. The pool will continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
Note that if this timeout value is greater than or equal to zero (0), and therefore an initial connection validation is performed, this timeout does not override the {@code connectionTimeout} or {@code validationTimeout}; they will be honored before this timeout is applied. The default value is one millisecond.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.metadata.redis.pool.max-idle

docs.description: Maximum amount of time (in milliseconds) a connection allocation should block before throwing an exception when the pool is exhausted. Use a negative value to block indefinitely.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.metadata.redis.pool.min-evictable-idle-time-millis
docs.description: Sets the minimum amount of time an object may sit idle in the pool before it is eligible for eviction by the idle object evictor (if any - see setTimeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis(long)). When non-positive, no objects will be evicted from the pool due to idle time alone.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.metadata.redis.pool.min-idle
docs.description: Target for the minimum number of idle connections to maintain in the pool. This setting only has an effect if it is positive.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.metadata.redis.pool.num-tests-per-eviction-run
docs.description: Sets the maximum number of objects to examine during each run (if any) of the idle object evictor thread. When positive, the number of tests performed for a run will be the minimum of the configured value and the number of idle instances in the pool. When negative, the number of tests performed will be ceil(getNumIdle()/ abs(getNumTestsPerEvictionRun())) which means that when the value is -n roughly one nth of the idle objects will be tested per run.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.metadata.redis.pool.soft-min-evictable-idle-time-millis
docs.description: Sets the minimum amount of time an object may sit idle in the pool before it is eligible for eviction by the idle object evictor (if any - see setTimeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis(long)), with the extra condition that at least minIdle object instances remain in the pool. This setting is overridden by getMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() (that is, if getMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() is positive, then getSoftMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() is ignored).

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.metadata.redis.pool.test-on-borrow
docs.description: Returns whether objects borrowed from the pool will be validated before being returned from the borrowObject() method. Validation is performed by the validateObject() method of the factory associated with the pool. If the object fails to validate, it will be removed from the pool and destroyed, and a new attempt will be made to borrow an object from the pool.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.metadata.redis.pool.test-on-create
docs.description: Returns whether objects created for the pool will be validated before being returned from the borrowObject() method. Validation is performed by the validateObject() method of the factory associated with the pool. If the object fails to validate, then borrowObject() will fail.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.metadata.redis.pool.test-on-return
docs.description: Returns whether objects borrowed from the pool will be validated when they are returned to the pool via the returnObject() method. Validation is performed by the validateObject() method of the factory associated with the pool. Returning objects that fail validation are destroyed rather then being returned the pool.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.metadata.redis.pool.test-while-idle
docs.description: Returns whether objects sitting idle in the pool will be validated by the idle object evictor ( if any - see setTimeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis(long)). Validation is performed by the validateObject() method of the factory associated with the pool. If the object fails to validate, it will be removed from the pool and destroyed.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.metadata.redis.pool.time-between-eviction-runs-millis
docs.description: Sets the amount of time (in milliseconds) between runs of the idle object evictor thread. When non-positive, no idle object evictor thread will be run. If positive, the idle object evictor thread will run at least once every timeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis milliseconds, and will attempt to evict objects from the pool that are idle longer than getMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() (if positive) or getSoftMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() (if positive).

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.metadata.redis.read-from
docs.description:
Setting that describes how Lettuce routes read operations to replica nodes. Note that modes referencing MASTER/SLAVE are deprecated (but still supported) in the Lettuce redis client dependency so migrate config to UPSTREAM/REPLICA. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code UPSTREAM}: Read from the current upstream node.
  • {@code UPSTREAMPREFERRED}: Read from the upstream node, but if it is unavailable, read from replica nodes.
  • {@code MASTER}: Read from the current upstream node.
  • {@code MASTERPREFERRED}: Read from the upstream node, but if it is unavailable, read from replica nodes.
  • {@code SLAVE}: Read from replica nodes.
  • {@code SLAVEPREFERRED}: Read from the replica nodes, but if none is unavailable, read from the upstream node.
  • {@code REPLICA}: Read from replica nodes.
  • {@code REPLICAPREFERRED}: Read from the replica nodes, but if none is unavailable, read from the upstream node.
  • {@code ANY}: Read from any node of the cluster.
  • {@code ANYREPLICA}: Read from any replica node of the cluster.
  • {@code NEAREST}: Read from the nearest node.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.metadata.redis.scan-count
docs.description: Redis scan count option. When and if specified, SCAN operations would be "counted" or limited by this setting. While SCAN does not provide guarantees about the number of elements returned at every iteration, it is possible to empirically adjust the behavior of SCAN using the COUNT option. Basically with COUNT the user specified the amount of work that should be done at every call in order to retrieve elements from the collection. This is just a hint for the implementation, however generally speaking this is what you could expect most of the times from the implementation.

docs.name: cas.authn.saml-idp.metadata.redis.share-native-connections
docs.description: The shared native connection is never closed by Lettuce connection, therefore it is not validated by default when connections are retrieved. If this setting is {@code true}, a shared connection will be used for regular operations and a connection provider will be used to select a connection for blocking and tx operations only, which should not share a connection. If native connection sharing is disabled, new (or pooled) connections will be used for all operations. By default, multiple connections share a single thread-safe native connection. If you enable connection pooling, then native connection sharing will be disabled and the connection pool will be used for all operations. You may however explicitly control connection sharing via this setting as an override.

  • {@code bindDn/bindCredential} set to {@code *} - Use a fast-bind strategy to initialize the pool.

  • {@code ROUND_ROBIN} For each new connection the next url in the list will be used.
  • {@code RANDOM} For each new connection a random LDAP url will be selected.
  • {@code DNS_SRV} LDAP urls based on DNS SRV records of the configured/given LDAP url will be used.
