docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed-idp.sts.crypto.strategy-type
docs.description:
Control the cipher sequence of operations. The accepted values are:
  • {@code ENCRYPT_AND_SIGN}: Encrypt the value first, and then sign.
  • {@code SIGN_AND_ENCRYPT}: Sign the value first, and then encrypt.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed-idp.sts.custom-claims
docs.description: Collection of fully-qualified claims prefixed with the appropriate namespace that are expected to be released via attribute release policy.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed-idp.sts.encrypt-tokens
docs.description: Whether tokens generated by STS should encrypted.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed-idp.sts.encryption-keystore-file
docs.description: Keystore path used to encrypt tokens.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed-idp.sts.encryption-keystore-password
docs.description: Keystore password used to encrypt tokens.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed-idp.sts.realm.issuer
docs.description: Issuer/name of the realm identified and registered with STS.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed-idp.sts.realm.key-password
docs.description: Key alias associated with the this realm.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed-idp.sts.realm.keystore-alias
docs.description: Key alias associated with the this realm.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed-idp.sts.realm.keystore-file
docs.description: Keystore path associated with the this realm.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed-idp.sts.realm.keystore-password
docs.description: Keystore password associated with the this realm.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed-idp.sts.sign-tokens
docs.description: Set whether the provided token will be signed or not. Default is true.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed-idp.sts.signing-keystore-file
docs.description: Keystore path used to sign tokens.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed-idp.sts.signing-keystore-password
docs.description: Keystore password used to sign tokens.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed-idp.sts.subject-name-id-format
docs.description:
When generating a SAML token, indicates the subject name-id format to use. Accepted values are:
  • unspecified
  • email
  • transient
  • persistent
  • entity

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed-idp.sts.subject-name-qualifier
docs.description: When generating a SAML token, indicates the subject name-id qualifier to use.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].attribute-mutator-script.location
docs.description:
Path to attribute mutator groovy script that allows one to modify wsfed attributes before establishing a final principal. The location of the resource. Resources can be URLs, or files found either on the classpath or outside somewhere in the file system.

In the event the configured resource is a Groovy script, especially if the script is set to reload on changes, you may need to adjust the total number of {@code inotify} instances. On Linux, you may need to add the following line to {@code /etc/sysctl.conf}: {@code fs.inotify.max_user_instances = 256}.

You can check the current value via {@code cat /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances}.

In situations and scenarios where CAS is able to automatically watch the underlying resource for changes and detect updates and modifications dynamically, you may be able to specify the following setting as either an environment variable or system property with a value of {@code false} to disable the resource watcher: {@code org.apereo.cas.util.io.PathWatcherService}.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].attribute-resolver-enabled
docs.description:
Whether CAS should enable its own attribute resolution machinery
after having received a response from wsfed.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].attributes-type
docs.description:
Indicates how attributes should be recorded into the principal object.
Useful if you wish to additionally resolve attributes on top of what wsfed provides.
Accepted values are {@code CAS,WSFED,BOTH}.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].auto-redirect-type
docs.description:
Whether CAS should auto redirect to this wsfed instance. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code SERVER}: Redirect on the server side, typically making CAS invisible.
  • {@code CLIENT}: Redirect on the client side using browser redirects, etc.
  • {@code NONE}: Do nothing and let the selection take place manually.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].cookie.allowed-ip-addresses-pattern
docs.description:
A regular expression pattern that indicates the set of allowed IP addresses,
when {@link #isPinToSession()} is configured. In the event that there is a mismatch
between the cookie IP address and the current request-provided IP address (i.e. network switches, VPN, etc),
the cookie can still be considered valid if the new IP address matches the pattern
specified here.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].cookie.crypto.alg
docs.description: The signing/encryption algorithm to use.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].cookie.crypto.enabled
docs.description: Whether crypto operations are enabled.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].cookie.crypto.encryption.key
docs.description: The encryption key is a string whose length is defined by the encryption key size setting.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].cookie.crypto.encryption.key-size
docs.description: The encryption key size.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].cookie.crypto.signing.key
docs.description: The signing key is a string whose length is defined by the signing key size setting.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].cookie.crypto.signing.key-size
docs.description: The signing key size.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].cookie.crypto.strategy-type
docs.description:
Control the cipher sequence of operations. The accepted values are:
  • {@code ENCRYPT_AND_SIGN}: Encrypt the value first, and then sign.
  • {@code SIGN_AND_ENCRYPT}: Sign the value first, and then encrypt.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].cookie.domain
docs.description:
Cookie domain. Specifies the domain within which this cookie should be presented.
The form of the domain name is specified by RFC 2965. A domain name begins with a dot (.foo.com)
and means that the cookie is visible to servers in a
specified Domain Name System (DNS) zone (for example, www.foo.com, but not a.b.foo.com).
By default, cookies are only returned to the server that sent them.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].cookie.geo-locate-client-session
docs.description:
When set to {@code true} and assuming {@link #isPinToSession()} is also {@code true},
client sessions (using the client IP address) are geo-located using a geolocation service when/if configured.
The resulting session is either pinned to the client geolocation, or the default client address.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].cookie.http-only
docs.description:
true if this cookie contains the HttpOnly attribute. This means that the cookie should
not be accessible to scripting engines, like javascript.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].cookie.max-age
docs.description:
The maximum age of the cookie, specified in seconds. By default, {@code -1} indicating
the cookie will persist until browser shutdown.
A positive value indicates that the cookie will expire after that many seconds have passed. Note that the value is
the maximum age when the cookie will expire, not the cookie's current age.
A negative value means that the cookie is not stored persistently and will be deleted when the Web browser exits.
A zero value causes the cookie to be deleted.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].cookie.name
docs.description:
Cookie name. Constructs a cookie with a specified name and value.
The name must conform to RFC 2965. That means it can contain only ASCII alphanumeric characters and
cannot contain commas, semicolons, or white space or begin with a {@code $} character.
The cookie's name cannot be changed after creation.
By default, cookies are created according to the RFC 2965 cookie specification.
Cookie names are automatically calculated assigned by CAS at runtime, and there is usually
no need to customize the name or assign it a different value unless a special use case warrants the change.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].cookie.path
docs.description:
Cookie path.
Specifies a path for the cookie to which the client should return the cookie.
The cookie is visible to all the pages in the directory you specify, and all the pages in that directory's
subdirectories. A cookie's path must include the servlet that set the cookie, for example, /catalog,
which makes the cookie visible to all directories on the server under /catalog.
Consult RFC 2965 (available on the Internet) for more information on setting path names for cookies.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].cookie.pin-to-session
docs.description:
When generating cookie values, determine whether the value should be compounded and signed with the properties of the current session, such as IP address, user-agent, etc.

Turning off session pinning is not exactly ideal. This is a barrier to prevent cookie replay attacks. A cookie that was created with an IP given a certain location cannot be replayed back in a different browser with a different IP from a different location.

There may however be legitimate reasons to turn it off and relax this after careful reviews, if you intend to support a type of user who intends to switch their IP quite frequently. A classic example is the type of user that is on VPN at the time of login, but decides to resume their work a few hours later off VPN or at a different location.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].cookie.same-site-policy
docs.description:
If a cookie is only intended to be accessed in a first party context, the developer has the option to apply one of settings {@code SameSite=Lax} or {@code SameSite=Strict} or {@code SameSite=None} to prevent external access.

To safeguard more websites and their users, the new secure-by-default model assumes all cookies should be protected from external access unless otherwise specified. Developers must use a new cookie setting, {@code SameSite=None}, to designate cookies for cross-site access. When the {@code SameSite=None} attribute is present, an additional {@code Secure} attribute is used so cross-site cookies can only be accessed over HTTPS connections.

Accepted values are:
  • {@code Lax}
  • {@code Strict}
  • {@code None}
  • {@code Off}: Disable the generation of the SameSite cookie attribute altogether.
  • Path to a Groovy script that is able to generate the SameSite cookie attribute dynamically.
  • Fully qualified name of a class that implements {@code org.apereo.cas.web.cookie.CookieSameSitePolicy}

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].cookie.secure
docs.description:
True if sending this cookie should be restricted to a secure protocol, or
false if the it can be sent using any protocol.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].encryption-certificate
docs.description: The path to the public key/certificate used to handle and verify encrypted assertions.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].encryption-private-key
docs.description: The path to the private key used to handle and verify encrypted assertions.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].encryption-private-key-password
docs.description: The private key password.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].id
docs.description:
Internal identifier for this wsfed configuration.
If undefined, the identifier would be auto-generated by CAS itself.
In the event that there is more than on CAS server defined in a clustered
deployment, this identifier must be statically defined in the configuration.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].identity-attribute
docs.description: The attribute extracted from the assertion and used to construct the CAS principal id.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].identity-provider-identifier
docs.description: The entity id or the identifier of the Wsfed instance.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].identity-provider-url
docs.description: Wsfed identity provider url.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].name
docs.description: Name of the authentication handler.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].order
docs.description: The order of the authentication handler in the chain.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].principal.active-attribute-repository-ids
docs.description:
Activated attribute repository identifiers
that should be used for fetching attributes
if attribute resolution is enabled.
The list here may include identifiers separated by comma.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].principal.attribute-repository-selection
docs.description:
Control the behavior of the attribute repository selection by authentication method or handler.
The map here is keyed by the authentication handler name, and the value is the attribute repository
identifiers separated by comma. When the authentication handler is executed, the attribute repositories
assigned to this handler will be selected to fetch attributes.
Note that the resolution engine will always favor attribute repositories assigned to the
service definition, if any and as part of its authentication policy, over this global setting.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].principal.attribute-resolution-enabled
docs.description:
Whether attribute repositories should be contacted to fetch person attributes. Defaults to true if not set. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code TRUE}: Constant to represent the true state.
  • {@code FALSE}: Constant to represent the false state.
  • {@code UNDEFINED}: Constant to represent the undefined state.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].principal.principal-attribute
docs.description:
Attribute name to use to indicate the identifier of the principal constructed.
If the attribute is blank or has no values, the default principal id will be used
determined by the underlying authentication engine. The principal id attribute
usually is removed from the collection of attributes collected, though this behavior
depends on the schematics of the underlying authentication strategy.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].principal.principal-resolution-conflict-strategy
docs.description:
In the event that the principal resolution engine resolves
more than one principal, (especially if such principals in the chain
have different identifiers), this setting determines strategy by which
the principal id would be chosen from the chain.
Accepted values are: {@code last}, {@code first}.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].principal.principal-resolution-failure-fatal
docs.description:
When true, throws an error back indicating that principal resolution has failed and no principal can be found based on the authentication requirements. Otherwise, logs the condition as an error without raising a catastrophic error. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code TRUE}: Constant to represent the true state.
  • {@code FALSE}: Constant to represent the false state.
  • {@code UNDEFINED}: Constant to represent the undefined state.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].principal.principal-transformation.blocking-pattern
docs.description:
A regular expression that will be used against the username
to match for blocking/forbidden values.
If a match is found, an exception will be thrown
and principal transformation will fail.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].principal.principal-transformation.case-conversion
docs.description:
Indicate whether the principal identifier should be transformed into upper-case, lower-case, etc. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code NONE}: No conversion.
  • {@code LOWERCASE}: Lowercase conversion.
  • {@code UPPERCASE}: Uppercase conversion.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].principal.principal-transformation.groovy.location
docs.description:
Transform usernames using a Groovy resource. The location of the resource. Resources can be URLs, or files found either on the classpath or outside somewhere in the file system.

In the event the configured resource is a Groovy script, especially if the script is set to reload on changes, you may need to adjust the total number of {@code inotify} instances. On Linux, you may need to add the following line to {@code /etc/sysctl.conf}: {@code fs.inotify.max_user_instances = 256}.

You can check the current value via {@code cat /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances}.

In situations and scenarios where CAS is able to automatically watch the underlying resource for changes and detect updates and modifications dynamically, you may be able to specify the following setting as either an environment variable or system property with a value of {@code false} to disable the resource watcher: {@code org.apereo.cas.util.io.PathWatcherService}.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].principal.principal-transformation.pattern
docs.description:
A regular expression that will be used against the provided username
for username extractions. On a successful match, the first matched group
in the pattern will be used as the extracted username.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].principal.principal-transformation.prefix
docs.description: Prefix to add to the principal id prior to authentication.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].principal.principal-transformation.suffix
docs.description: Suffix to add to the principal id prior to authentication.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].principal.return-null
docs.description:
Return a null principal object if no attributes can be found for the principal. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code TRUE}: Constant to represent the true state.
  • {@code FALSE}: Constant to represent the false state.
  • {@code UNDEFINED}: Constant to represent the undefined state.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].principal.use-existing-principal-id
docs.description:
Uses an existing principal id that may have already been established in order to run person directory queries. This is generally useful in situations where authentication is delegated to an external identity provider and a principal is first established to then query an attribute source. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code TRUE}: Constant to represent the true state.
  • {@code FALSE}: Constant to represent the false state.
  • {@code UNDEFINED}: Constant to represent the undefined state.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].relying-party-identifier
docs.description: The identifier for CAS (RP) registered with wsfed.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].signing-certificate-resources
docs.description:
Locations of signing certificates used to verify assertions.
Locations could be specified as static file-system resources(certificates)
or they could also be federation XML metadata, either as a URL or an XML file.
If federation metadata XML is provided, the signing certificate is extracted
from the {@code IDPSSODescriptor}'s key descriptor that is marked for signing.

docs.name: cas.authn.wsfed[].tolerance
docs.description: Tolerance value used to skew assertions to support clock drift.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.cache-max-elements-in-memory
docs.description: When CRLs are cached, indicate maximum number of elements kept in memory.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.cache-time-to-live-seconds
docs.description: When CRLs are cached, indicate the time-to-live of cache items.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.check-all
docs.description: Whether revocation checking should check all resources, or stop at first one.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.check-key-usage
docs.description: Deployer supplied setting to check the KeyUsage extension.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.cn-edipi.alternate-principal-attribute
docs.description:
Attribute name that will be used by X509 principal resolvers if the main attribute in the certificate is not present. This only applies to principal resolvers that are looking for attributes in the certificate that are not common to all certificates. (e.g. {@code SUBJECT_ALT_NAME}, {@code CN_EDIPI})

This assumes you would rather get something like the {@code subjectDn} rather than {@code null} where {@code null} would allow falling through to another authentication mechanism.

Currently supported values are: {@code subjectDn}, {@code sigAlgOid}, {@code subjectX500Principal}.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.cn-edipi.extract-edipi-as-attribute
docs.description: Whether to extract EDIPI as an attribute, regardless of principal resolver type.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.crl-expired-policy
docs.description:
If the CRL has expired, activate the this policy. Activated if {@link #revocationChecker} is {@code CRL}. Accepted values are:
  • {@code ALLOW}: Allow authentication to proceed.
  • {@code DENY}: Deny authentication and block.
  • {@code THRESHOLD}: Applicable to CRL expiration, throttle the request whereby expired data is permitted up to a threshold period of time but not afterward.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.crl-fetcher
docs.description:
Options to describe how to fetch CRL resources.

To fetch CRLs, the following options are available:

  • {@code RESOURCE}: By default, all revocation checks use fixed resources to fetch the CRL resource from the specified location.
  • {@code LDAP}: A CRL resource may be fetched from a pre-configured attribute, in the event that the CRL resource location is an LDAP URI.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.crl-resource-expired-policy
docs.description:
If the CRL resource has expired, activate the this policy. Activated if {@link #revocationChecker} is {@code RESOURCE}. Accepted values are:
  • {@code ALLOW}: Allow authentication to proceed.
  • {@code DENY}: Deny authentication and block.
  • {@code THRESHOLD}: Applicable to CRL expiration, throttle the request whereby expired data is permitted up to a threshold period of time but not afterward.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.crl-resource-unavailable-policy
docs.description:
If the CRL resource is unavailable, activate the this policy. Activated if {@link #revocationChecker} is {@code RESOURCE}. Accepted values are:
  • {@code ALLOW}: Allow authentication to proceed.
  • {@code DENY}: Deny authentication and block.
  • {@code THRESHOLD}: Applicable to CRL expiration, throttle the request whereby expired data is permitted up to a threshold period of time but not afterward.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.crl-resources
docs.description: List of CRL resources to use for fetching.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.crl-unavailable-policy
docs.description:
If the CRL is unavailable, activate the this policy. Activated if {@link #revocationChecker} is {@code CRL}. Accepted values are:
  • {@code ALLOW}: Allow authentication to proceed.
  • {@code DENY}: Deny authentication and block.
  • {@code THRESHOLD}: Applicable to CRL expiration, throttle the request whereby expired data is permitted up to a threshold period of time but not afterward.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.extract-cert
docs.description: Whether to extract certificate from request. The default implementation extracts certificate from header via Tomcat SSLValve parsing logic and using the {@link #DEFAULT_CERT_HEADER_NAME} header. Must be false by default because if someone enables it they need to make sure they are behind proxy that won't let the header arrive directly from the browser.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.allow-multiple-dns
docs.description: Whether search/query results are allowed to match on multiple DNs, or whether a single unique DN is expected for the result.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.allow-multiple-entries
docs.description: Set if multiple Entries are allowed.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.base-dn
docs.description: Base DN to use. There may be scenarios where different parts of a single LDAP tree could be considered as base-dns. Rather than duplicating the LDAP configuration block for each individual base-dn, each entry can be specified and joined together using a special delimiter character. The user DN is retrieved using the combination of all base-dn and DN resolvers in the order defined. DN resolution should fail if multiple DNs are found. Otherwise the first DN found is returned. Usual syntax is: {@code subtreeA,dc=example,dc=net|subtreeC,dc=example,dc=net}.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.binary-attributes
docs.description: Indicate the collection of attributes that are to be tagged and processed as binary attributes by the underlying search resolver.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.bind-credential
docs.description: The bind credential to use when connecting to LDAP.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.bind-dn
docs.description:
The bind DN to use when connecting to LDAP. LDAP connection configuration injected into the LDAP connection pool can be initialized with the following parameters:
  • {@code bindDn/bindCredential} provided - Use the provided credentials to bind when initializing connections.
  • {@code bindDn/bindCredential} set to {@code *} - Use a fast-bind strategy to initialize the pool.
  • {@code bindDn/bindCredential} set to blank - Skip connection initializing; perform operations anonymously.
  • SASL mechanism provided - Use the given SASL mechanism to bind when initializing connections.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.block-wait-time
docs.description: The length of time the pool will block. By default the pool will block indefinitely and there is no guarantee that waiting threads will be serviced in the order in which they made their request. This option should be used with a blocking connection pool when you need to control the exact number of connections that can be created

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.certificate-attribute
docs.description: The LDAP attribute that holds the certificate revocation list.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.connect-timeout
docs.description: Sets the maximum amount of time that connects will block.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.connection-strategy
docs.description:
If multiple URLs are provided as the ldapURL this describes how each URL will be processed.
  • {@code ACTIVE_PASSIVE} First LDAP will be used for every request unless it fails and then the next shall be used.
  • {@code ROUND_ROBIN} For each new connection the next url in the list will be used.
  • {@code RANDOM} For each new connection a random LDAP url will be selected.
  • {@code DNS_SRV} LDAP urls based on DNS SRV records of the configured/given LDAP url will be used.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.disable-pooling
docs.description: Whether to use a pooled connection factory in components.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.fail-fast
docs.description: Attempt to populate the connection pool early on startup and fail quickly if something goes wrong.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.follow-referrals
docs.description: Set if search referrals should be followed.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.hostname-verifier
docs.description:
Hostname verification options. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code DEFAULT}: Default option, forcing verification.
  • {@code ANY}: Skip hostname verification and allow all.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.idle-time
docs.description: Removes connections from the pool based on how long they have been idle in the available queue. Prunes connections that have been idle for more than the indicated amount.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.keystore
docs.description: Path to the keystore used for SSL connections. Typically contains SSL certificates for the LDAP server.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.keystore-password
docs.description: Keystore password.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.keystore-type
docs.description: The type of keystore. {@code PKCS12} or {@code JKS}. If left blank, defaults to the default keystore type indicated by the underlying Java platform.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.ldap-url
docs.description: The LDAP url to the server. More than one may be specified, separated by space and/or comma.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.max-pool-size
docs.description: Maximum LDAP connection pool size which the pool can use to grow.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.min-pool-size
docs.description: Minimum LDAP connection pool size. Size the pool should be initialized to and pruned to

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.name
docs.description: Name of the LDAP handler.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.page-size
docs.description: Request that the server return results in batches of a specific size. See RFC 2696. This control is often used to work around server result size limits. A negative/zero value disables paged requests.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.pool-passivator
docs.description:
You may receive unexpected LDAP failures, when CAS is configured to authenticate using {@code DIRECT} or {@code AUTHENTICATED} types and LDAP is locked down to not allow anonymous binds/searches. Every second attempt with a given LDAP connection from the pool would fail if it was on the same connection as a failed login attempt, and the regular connection validator would similarly fail. When a connection is returned back to a pool, it still may contain the principal and credentials from the previous attempt. Before the next bind attempt using that connection, the validator tries to validate the connection again but fails because it’s no longer trying with the configured bind credentials but with whatever user DN was used in the previous step. Given the validation failure, the connection is closed and CAS would deny access by default. Passivators attempt to reconnect to LDAP with the configured bind credentials, effectively resetting the connection to what it should be after each bind request. Furthermore if you are seeing errors in the logs that resemble a 'Operation exception encountered, reopening connection' type of message, this usually is an indication that the connection pool’s validation timeout established and created by CAS is greater than the timeout configured in the LDAP server, or more likely, in the load balancer in front of the LDAP servers. You can adjust the LDAP server session’s timeout for connections, or you can teach CAS to use a validity period that is equal or less than the LDAP server session’s timeout. Accepted values are:
  • {@code NONE}: No passivation takes place.
  • {@code BIND}: The default behavior which passivates a connection by performing a bind operation on it. This option requires the availability of bind credentials when establishing connections to LDAP.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.prune-period
docs.description: Removes connections from the pool based on how long they have been idle in the available queue. Run the pruning process at the indicated interval.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.response-timeout
docs.description: Duration of time to wait for responses.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.sasl-authorization-id
docs.description: SASL authorization id.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.ldap.search-entry-handlers[].type
docs.description:
The type of search entry handler to choose. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code FOLLOW_SEARCH_REFERRAL}: Provides handling of an ldap referral for search operations.
  • {@code FOLLOW_SEARCH_RESULT_REFERENCE}: Provides handling of an ldap continuation reference for search operations.
  • {@code ACTIVE_DIRECTORY}: Process the entry results fetched from active directory and check for account status controls for disabled/expired accounts, etc.
  • {@code OBJECT_GUID}: Object guid search entry handler. Handles the {@code objectGUID} attribute fetching and conversion.
  • {@code OBJECT_SID}: Object sid search entry handler. Handles the {@code objectSid} attribute fetching and conversion.
  • {@code CASE_CHANGE}: Case change search entry handler. Provides the ability to modify the case of search entry DNs, attribute names, and attribute values.
  • {@code DN_ATTRIBUTE_ENTRY}: DN attribute entry handler. Adds the entry DN as an attribute to the result set. Provides a client side implementation of RFC 5020.
  • {@code MERGE}: Merge search entry handler. Merges the values of one or more attributes into a single attribute.
  • {@code PRIMARY_GROUP}: Primary group search handler. Constructs the primary group SID and then searches for that group and puts it's DN in the {@code memberOf} attribute of the original search entry.
  • {@code RANGE_ENTRY}: Range entry search handler. Rewrites attributes returned from Active Directory to include all values by performing additional searches.
  • {@code RECURSIVE_ENTRY}: Recursive entry search handler. This recursively searches based on a supplied attribute and merges those results into the original entry.
  • {@code MERGE_ENTRIES}: Merge entries handler. Merges the values of one or more attributes in all entries into a single attribute. The merged attribute may or may not already exist on the entry. If it does exist it's existing values will remain intact.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.principal-type
docs.description:
Indicates the type of principal resolution for X509. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code CN_EDIPI}: Create principal by common name and EDIPI.
  • {@code RFC822_EMAIL}: Create principal from the RFC822 type name (aka email address) in the subject alternative name field. The subject alternative name field contains a list of various types of names, one type is RFC822 e-mail address. This will return the first e-mail address that is found (if there are more than one).
  • {@code SERIAL_NO}: Create principal by serial no. Resolve the principal by the serial number with a configurable radix, ranging from 2 to 36. If {@code radix} is {@code 16}, then the serial number could be filled with leading zeros to even the number of digits.
  • {@code SERIAL_NO_DN}: Create principal by serial no and DN.
  • {@code SUBJECT}: Create principal by subject. Resolve the principal by extracting one or more attribute values from the certificate subject DN and combining them with intervening delimiters.
  • {@code SUBJECT_ALT_NAME}: Create principal by subject alternative name. Resolve the principal by the subject alternative name extension. (type: otherName).
  • {@code SUBJECT_DN}: Create principal by subject DN.

docs.description: Control the behavior of the attribute repository selection by authentication method or handler. The map here is keyed by the authentication handler name, and the value is the attribute repository identifiers separated by comma. When the authentication handler is executed, the attribute repositories assigned to this handler will be selected to fetch attributes. Note that the resolution engine will always favor attribute repositories assigned to the service definition, if any and as part of its authentication policy, over this global setting.

The principal id attribute usually is removed from the collection of attributes collected, though this behavior depends on the schematics of the underlying authentication strategy.

docs.name: cas.authn.x509.subject-dn.format
docs.description:
Format of subject DN to use. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code DEFAULT}: Denigrated result of calling certificate.getSubjectDN() method. Javadocs designate this method as "denigrated" for not being portable and/or not being well defined. It is what has been used by CAS for a long time so it remains the default.
  • {@code RFC1779}: RFC 1779 String format of Distinguished Names. Calls {@code X500Principal.getName("RFC1779")} which emits a subject DN with the attribute keywords defined in RFC 1779 (CN, L, ST, O, OU, C, STREET). Any other attribute type is emitted as an OID.
  • {@code RFC2253}: RFC 2253 String format of Distinguished Names. Calls {@code X500Principal.getName("RFC2253")} which emits a subject DN with the attribute keywords defined in RFC 2253 (CN, L, ST, O, OU, C, STREET, DC, UID). Any other attribute type is emitted as an OID.
  • {@code CANONICAL}: Canonical String format of Distinguished Names. Calls X500Principal.getName("CANONICAL" which emits a subject DN that starts with RFC 2253 and applies additional canonicalization described in the javadoc.

docs.name: cas.consent.dynamo-db.billing-mode
docs.description:
Billing mode specifies how you are charged for read and write throughput and how you manage capacity. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code PROVISIONED}: Provisioned mode means that you specify the number of reads and writes per second that you expect your application to use. Provisioned mode is a good option if any of the following are true:
    • You have predictable application traffic.
    • You run applications whose traffic is consistent or ramps gradually.
    • You can forecast capacity requirements to control costs.
    You can use auto scaling to automatically adjust capacity based on the specified utilization rate to ensure application performance while reducing costs.
  • {@code PAY_PER_REQUEST}: Pay-per-request or on-demand billing means that you're charged for only the read/write requests that you use. On-demand mode is a good option if any of the following are true:
    • You create new tables with unknown workloads.
    • You have unpredictable application traffic.
    • You prefer the ease of paying for only what you use.
    Tables using on-demand mode support all DynamoDB features (such as encryption at rest, point-in-time recovery, global tables, and so on) with the exception of auto scaling, which is not applicable with this mode.

docs.name: cas.consent.jpa.ddl-auto
docs.description:
Hibernate feature to automatically validate and exports DDL to the schema. By default, creates and drops the schema automatically when a session is starts and ends. Setting the value to {@code validate} or {@code none} may be more desirable for production, but any of the following options can be used:
  • {@code validate}: Validate the schema, but make no changes to the database.
  • {@code update}: Update the schema.
  • {@code create}: Create the schema, destroying previous data.
  • {@code create-drop}: Drop the schema at the end of the session.
  • {@code none}: Do nothing.

Note that during a version migration where any schema has changed {@code create-drop} will result in the loss of all data as soon as CAS is started. For transient data like tickets this is probably not an issue, but in cases like the audit table important data could be lost. Using `update`, while safe for data, is confirmed to result in invalid database state. {@code validate} or {@code none} settings are likely the only safe options for production use.

For more info, see this.

docs.name: cas.consent.jpa.fail-fast-timeout
docs.description:
Set the pool initialization failure timeout.
  • Any value greater than zero will be treated as a timeout for pool initialization. The calling thread will be blocked from continuing until a successful connection to the database, or until the timeout is reached. If the timeout is reached, then a {@code PoolInitializationException} will be thrown.
  • A value of zero will not prevent the pool from starting in the case that a connection cannot be obtained. However, upon start the pool will attempt to obtain a connection and validate that the {@code connectionTestQuery} and {@code connectionInitSql} are valid. If those validations fail, an exception will be thrown. If a connection cannot be obtained, the validation is skipped and the pool will start and continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
  • A value less than zero will not bypass any connection attempt and validation during startup, and therefore the pool will start immediately. The pool will continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
Note that if this timeout value is greater than or equal to zero (0), and therefore an initial connection validation is performed, this timeout does not override the {@code connectionTimeout} or {@code validationTimeout}; they will be honored before this timeout is applied. The default value is one millisecond.

docs.name: cas.consent.ldap.pool-passivator
docs.description:
You may receive unexpected LDAP failures, when CAS is configured to authenticate using {@code DIRECT} or {@code AUTHENTICATED} types and LDAP is locked down to not allow anonymous binds/searches. Every second attempt with a given LDAP connection from the pool would fail if it was on the same connection as a failed login attempt, and the regular connection validator would similarly fail. When a connection is returned back to a pool, it still may contain the principal and credentials from the previous attempt. Before the next bind attempt using that connection, the validator tries to validate the connection again but fails because it’s no longer trying with the configured bind credentials but with whatever user DN was used in the previous step. Given the validation failure, the connection is closed and CAS would deny access by default. Passivators attempt to reconnect to LDAP with the configured bind credentials, effectively resetting the connection to what it should be after each bind request. Furthermore if you are seeing errors in the logs that resemble a 'Operation exception encountered, reopening connection' type of message, this usually is an indication that the connection pool’s validation timeout established and created by CAS is greater than the timeout configured in the LDAP server, or more likely, in the load balancer in front of the LDAP servers. You can adjust the LDAP server session’s timeout for connections, or you can teach CAS to use a validity period that is equal or less than the LDAP server session’s timeout. Accepted values are:
  • {@code NONE}: No passivation takes place.
  • {@code BIND}: The default behavior which passivates a connection by performing a bind operation on it. This option requires the availability of bind credentials when establishing connections to LDAP.

docs.name: cas.consent.ldap.search-entry-handlers[].type
docs.description:
The type of search entry handler to choose. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code FOLLOW_SEARCH_REFERRAL}: Provides handling of an ldap referral for search operations.
  • {@code FOLLOW_SEARCH_RESULT_REFERENCE}: Provides handling of an ldap continuation reference for search operations.
  • {@code ACTIVE_DIRECTORY}: Process the entry results fetched from active directory and check for account status controls for disabled/expired accounts, etc.
  • {@code OBJECT_GUID}: Object guid search entry handler. Handles the {@code objectGUID} attribute fetching and conversion.
  • {@code OBJECT_SID}: Object sid search entry handler. Handles the {@code objectSid} attribute fetching and conversion.
  • {@code CASE_CHANGE}: Case change search entry handler. Provides the ability to modify the case of search entry DNs, attribute names, and attribute values.
  • {@code DN_ATTRIBUTE_ENTRY}: DN attribute entry handler. Adds the entry DN as an attribute to the result set. Provides a client side implementation of RFC 5020.
  • {@code MERGE}: Merge search entry handler. Merges the values of one or more attributes into a single attribute.
  • {@code PRIMARY_GROUP}: Primary group search handler. Constructs the primary group SID and then searches for that group and puts it's DN in the {@code memberOf} attribute of the original search entry.
  • {@code RANGE_ENTRY}: Range entry search handler. Rewrites attributes returned from Active Directory to include all values by performing additional searches.
  • {@code RECURSIVE_ENTRY}: Recursive entry search handler. This recursively searches based on a supplied attribute and merges those results into the original entry.
  • {@code MERGE_ENTRIES}: Merge entries handler. Merges the values of one or more attributes in all entries into a single attribute. The merged attribute may or may not already exist on the entry. If it does exist it's existing values will remain intact.

docs.name: cas.consent.redis.pool.min-evictable-idle-time-millis
docs.description: Sets the minimum amount of time an object may sit idle in the pool before it is eligible for eviction by the idle object evictor (if any - see setTimeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis(long)). When non-positive, no objects will be evicted from the pool due to idle time alone.

docs.name: cas.consent.redis.pool.min-idle
docs.description: Target for the minimum number of idle connections to maintain in the pool. This setting only has an effect if it is positive.

docs.name: cas.consent.redis.pool.num-tests-per-eviction-run
docs.description: Sets the maximum number of objects to examine during each run (if any) of the idle object evictor thread. When positive, the number of tests performed for a run will be the minimum of the configured value and the number of idle instances in the pool. When negative, the number of tests performed will be ceil(getNumIdle()/ abs(getNumTestsPerEvictionRun())) which means that when the value is -n roughly one nth of the idle objects will be tested per run.

docs.name: cas.consent.redis.pool.soft-min-evictable-idle-time-millis
docs.description: Sets the minimum amount of time an object may sit idle in the pool before it is eligible for eviction by the idle object evictor (if any - see setTimeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis(long)), with the extra condition that at least minIdle object instances remain in the pool. This setting is overridden by getMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() (that is, if getMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() is positive, then getSoftMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() is ignored).

docs.name: cas.consent.redis.pool.test-on-borrow
docs.description: Returns whether objects borrowed from the pool will be validated before being returned from the borrowObject() method. Validation is performed by the validateObject() method of the factory associated with the pool. If the object fails to validate, it will be removed from the pool and destroyed, and a new attempt will be made to borrow an object from the pool.

docs.name: cas.consent.redis.pool.test-on-create
docs.description: Returns whether objects created for the pool will be validated before being returned from the borrowObject() method. Validation is performed by the validateObject() method of the factory associated with the pool. If the object fails to validate, then borrowObject() will fail.

docs.name: cas.consent.redis.pool.test-on-return
docs.description: Returns whether objects borrowed from the pool will be validated when they are returned to the pool via the returnObject() method. Validation is performed by the validateObject() method of the factory associated with the pool. Returning objects that fail validation are destroyed rather then being returned the pool.

docs.name: cas.consent.redis.pool.test-while-idle
docs.description: Returns whether objects sitting idle in the pool will be validated by the idle object evictor ( if any - see setTimeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis(long)). Validation is performed by the validateObject() method of the factory associated with the pool. If the object fails to validate, it will be removed from the pool and destroyed.

docs.name: cas.consent.redis.pool.time-between-eviction-runs-millis
docs.description: Sets the amount of time (in milliseconds) between runs of the idle object evictor thread. When non-positive, no idle object evictor thread will be run. If positive, the idle object evictor thread will run at least once every timeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis milliseconds, and will attempt to evict objects from the pool that are idle longer than getMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() (if positive) or getSoftMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() (if positive).

docs.name: cas.consent.redis.read-from
docs.description:
Setting that describes how Lettuce routes read operations to replica nodes. Note that modes referencing MASTER/SLAVE are deprecated (but still supported) in the Lettuce redis client dependency so migrate config to UPSTREAM/REPLICA. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code UPSTREAM}: Read from the current upstream node.
  • {@code UPSTREAMPREFERRED}: Read from the upstream node, but if it is unavailable, read from replica nodes.
  • {@code MASTER}: Read from the current upstream node.
  • {@code MASTERPREFERRED}: Read from the upstream node, but if it is unavailable, read from replica nodes.
  • {@code SLAVE}: Read from replica nodes.
  • {@code SLAVEPREFERRED}: Read from the replica nodes, but if none is unavailable, read from the upstream node.
  • {@code REPLICA}: Read from replica nodes.
  • {@code REPLICAPREFERRED}: Read from the replica nodes, but if none is unavailable, read from the upstream node.
  • {@code ANY}: Read from any node of the cluster.
  • {@code ANYREPLICA}: Read from any replica node of the cluster.
  • {@code NEAREST}: Read from the nearest node.

docs.name: cas.consent.redis.scan-count

While SCAN does not provide guarantees about the number of elements returned at every iteration, it is possible to empirically adjust the behavior of SCAN using the COUNT option. Basically with COUNT the user specified the amount of work that should be done at every call in order to retrieve elements from the collection. This is just a hint for the implementation, however generally speaking this is what you could expect most of the times from the implementation.

docs.name: cas.consent.redis.share-native-connections

If this setting is {@code true}, a shared connection will be used for regular operations and a connection provider will be used to select a connection for blocking and tx operations only, which should not share a connection. If native connection sharing is disabled, new (or pooled) connections will be used for all operations. By default, multiple connections share a single thread-safe native connection. If you enable connection pooling, then native connection sharing will be disabled and the connection pool will be used for all operations. You may however explicitly control connection sharing via this setting as an override.

docs.name: cas.events.dynamo-db.billing-mode
docs.description:
Billing mode specifies how you are charged for read and write throughput and how you manage capacity. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code PROVISIONED}: Provisioned mode means that you specify the number of reads and writes per second that you expect your application to use. Provisioned mode is a good option if any of the following are true:
    • You have predictable application traffic.
    • You run applications whose traffic is consistent or ramps gradually.
    • You can forecast capacity requirements to control costs.
    You can use auto scaling to automatically adjust capacity based on the specified utilization rate to ensure application performance while reducing costs.
  • {@code PAY_PER_REQUEST}: Pay-per-request or on-demand billing means that you're charged for only the read/write requests that you use. On-demand mode is a good option if any of the following are true:
    • You create new tables with unknown workloads.
    • You have unpredictable application traffic.
    • You prefer the ease of paying for only what you use.
    Tables using on-demand mode support all DynamoDB features (such as encryption at rest, point-in-time recovery, global tables, and so on) with the exception of auto scaling, which is not applicable with this mode.

docs.name: cas.events.jpa.ddl-auto
docs.description:
Hibernate feature to automatically validate and exports DDL to the schema. By default, creates and drops the schema automatically when a session is starts and ends. Setting the value to {@code validate} or {@code none} may be more desirable for production, but any of the following options can be used:
  • {@code validate}: Validate the schema, but make no changes to the database.
  • {@code update}: Update the schema.
  • {@code create}: Create the schema, destroying previous data.
  • {@code create-drop}: Drop the schema at the end of the session.
  • {@code none}: Do nothing.

Note that during a version migration where any schema has changed {@code create-drop} will result in the loss of all data as soon as CAS is started. For transient data like tickets this is probably not an issue, but in cases like the audit table important data could be lost. Using `update`, while safe for data, is confirmed to result in invalid database state. {@code validate} or {@code none} settings are likely the only safe options for production use.

For more info, see this.

Set the pool initialization failure timeout.

The calling thread will be blocked from continuing until a successful connection to the database, or until the timeout is reached. If the timeout is reached, then a {@code PoolInitializationException} will be thrown.
  • A value of zero will not prevent the pool from starting in the case that a connection cannot be obtained. However, upon start the pool will attempt to obtain a connection and validate that the {@code connectionTestQuery} and {@code connectionInitSql} are valid. If those validations fail, an exception will be thrown. If a connection cannot be obtained, the validation is skipped and the pool will start and continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
  • A value less than zero will not bypass any connection attempt and validation during startup, and therefore the pool will start immediately. The pool will continue to try to obtain connections in the background. This can mean that callers to {@code DataSource#getConnection()} may encounter exceptions.
Note that if this timeout value is greater than or equal to zero (0), and therefore an initial connection validation is performed, this timeout does not override the {@code connectionTimeout} or {@code validationTimeout}; they will be honored before this timeout is applied. The default value is one millisecond.

docs.name: cas.events.redis.pool.max-idle

docs.name: cas.events.redis.pool.max-wait
docs.description: Maximum amount of time (in milliseconds) a connection allocation should block before throwing an exception when the pool is exhausted. Use a negative value to block indefinitely.

docs.name: cas.events.redis.pool.min-evictable-idle-time-millis
docs.description: Sets the minimum amount of time an object may sit idle in the pool before it is eligible for eviction by the idle object evictor (if any - see setTimeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis(long)). When non-positive, no objects will be evicted from the pool due to idle time alone.

docs.name: cas.events.redis.pool.min-idle
docs.description: Target for the minimum number of idle connections to maintain in the pool. This setting only has an effect if it is positive.

docs.name: cas.events.redis.pool.num-tests-per-eviction-run
docs.description: Sets the maximum number of objects to examine during each run (if any) of the idle object evictor thread. When positive, the number of tests performed for a run will be the minimum of the configured value and the number of idle instances in the pool. When negative, the number of tests performed will be ceil(getNumIdle()/ abs(getNumTestsPerEvictionRun())) which means that when the value is -n roughly one nth of the idle objects will be tested per run.

docs.name: cas.events.redis.pool.soft-min-evictable-idle-time-millis
docs.description: Sets the minimum amount of time an object may sit idle in the pool before it is eligible for eviction by the idle object evictor (if any - see setTimeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis(long)), with the extra condition that at least minIdle object instances remain in the pool. This setting is overridden by getMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() (that is, if getMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() is positive, then getSoftMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() is ignored).

docs.name: cas.events.redis.pool.test-on-borrow
docs.description: Returns whether objects borrowed from the pool will be validated before being returned from the borrowObject() method. Validation is performed by the validateObject() method of the factory associated with the pool. If the object fails to validate, it will be removed from the pool and destroyed, and a new attempt will be made to borrow an object from the pool.

docs.name: cas.events.redis.pool.test-on-create
docs.description: Returns whether objects created for the pool will be validated before being returned from the borrowObject() method. Validation is performed by the validateObject() method of the factory associated with the pool. If the object fails to validate, then borrowObject() will fail.

docs.name: cas.events.redis.pool.test-on-return
docs.description: Returns whether objects borrowed from the pool will be validated when they are returned to the pool via the returnObject() method. Validation is performed by the validateObject() method of the factory associated with the pool. Returning objects that fail validation are destroyed rather then being returned the pool.

docs.name: cas.events.redis.pool.test-while-idle
docs.description: Returns whether objects sitting idle in the pool will be validated by the idle object evictor ( if any - see setTimeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis(long)). Validation is performed by the validateObject() method of the factory associated with the pool. If the object fails to validate, it will be removed from the pool and destroyed.

docs.name: cas.events.redis.pool.time-between-eviction-runs-millis
docs.description: Sets the amount of time (in milliseconds) between runs of the idle object evictor thread. When non-positive, no idle object evictor thread will be run. If positive, the idle object evictor thread will run at least once every timeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis milliseconds, and will attempt to evict objects from the pool that are idle longer than getMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() (if positive) or getSoftMinEvictableIdleTimeMillis() (if positive).

docs.name: cas.events.redis.read-from
docs.description:
Setting that describes how Lettuce routes read operations to replica nodes. Note that modes referencing MASTER/SLAVE are deprecated (but still supported) in the Lettuce redis client dependency so migrate config to UPSTREAM/REPLICA. Available values are as follows:
  • {@code UPSTREAM}: Read from the current upstream node.
  • {@code UPSTREAMPREFERRED}: Read from the upstream node, but if it is unavailable, read from replica nodes.
  • {@code MASTER}: Read from the current upstream node.
  • {@code MASTERPREFERRED}: Read from the upstream node, but if it is unavailable, read from replica nodes.
  • {@code SLAVE}: Read from replica nodes.
  • {@code SLAVEPREFERRED}: Read from the replica nodes, but if none is unavailable, read from the upstream node.
  • {@code REPLICA}: Read from replica nodes.
  • {@code REPLICAPREFERRED}: Read from the replica nodes, but if none is unavailable, read from the upstream node.
  • {@code ANY}: Read from any node of the cluster.
  • {@code ANYREPLICA}: Read from any replica node of the cluster.
  • {@code NEAREST}: Read from the nearest node.

docs.name: cas.events.redis.scan-count

While SCAN does not provide guarantees about the number of elements returned at every iteration, it is possible to empirically adjust the behavior of SCAN using the COUNT option. Basically with COUNT the user specified the amount of work that should be done at every call in order to retrieve elements from the collection. This is just a hint for the implementation, however generally speaking this is what you could expect most of the times from the implementation.

docs.name: cas.events.redis.share-native-connections
docs.description: The shared native connection is never closed by Lettuce connection, therefore it is not validated by default when connections are retrieved. If this setting is {@code true}, a shared connection will be used for regular operations and a connection provider will be used to select a connection for blocking and tx operations only, which should not share a connection. If native connection sharing is disabled, new (or pooled) connections will be used for all operations. By default, multiple connections share a single thread-safe native connection. If you enable connection pooling, then native connection sharing will be disabled and the connection pool will be used for all operations. You may however explicitly control connection sharing via this setting as an override.

In the event the configured resource is a Groovy script, especially if the script is set to reload on changes, you may need to adjust the total number of {@code inotify} instances. docs.name: cas.google-analytics.cookie.domain
docs.description: Cookie domain. Specifies the domain within which this cookie should be presented. The form of the domain name is specified by RFC 2965. A domain name begins with a dot (.foo.com) and means that the cookie is visible to servers in a specified Domain Name System (DNS) zone (for example, www.foo.com, but not a.b.foo.com). By default, cookies are only returned to the server that sent them.

docs.name: cas.google-analytics.cookie.http-only
docs.description: true if this cookie contains the HttpOnly attribute. This means that the cookie should not be accessible to scripting engines, like javascript.

docs.name: cas.google-analytics.cookie.max-age
docs.description: The maximum age of the cookie, specified in seconds. By default, {@code -1} indicating the cookie will persist until browser shutdown. A positive value indicates that the cookie will expire after that many seconds have passed. Note that the value is the maximum age when the cookie will expire, not the cookie's current age. A negative value means that the cookie is not stored persistently and will be deleted when the Web browser exits. A zero value causes the cookie to be deleted.

docs.name: cas.google-analytics.cookie.name
docs.description: Cookie name. Constructs a cookie with a specified name and value. The name must conform to RFC 2965. That means it can contain only ASCII alphanumeric characters and cannot contain commas, semicolons, or white space or begin with a {@code $} character. The cookie's name cannot be changed after creation. By default, cookies are created according to the RFC 2965 cookie specification. Cookie names are automatically calculated assigned by CAS at runtime, and there is usually no need to customize the name or assign it a different value unless a special use case warrants the change.

docs.name: cas.google-analytics.cookie.path
docs.description: Cookie path. Specifies a path for the cookie to which the client should return the cookie. The cookie is visible to all the pages in the directory you specify, and all the pages in that directory's subdirectories. A cookie's path must include the servlet that set the cookie, for example, /catalog, which makes the cookie visible to all directories on the server under /catalog. Consult RFC 2965 (available on the Internet) for more information on setting path names for cookies.

docs.name: cas.google-analytics.cookie.same-site-policy
docs.description:
If a cookie is only intended to be accessed in a first party context, the developer has the option to apply one of settings {@code SameSite=Lax} or {@code SameSite=Strict} or {@code SameSite=None} to prevent external access.

To safeguard more websites and their users, the new secure-by-default model assumes all cookies should be protected from external access unless otherwise specified. Developers must use a new cookie setting, {@code SameSite=None}, to designate cookies for cross-site access. When the {@code SameSite=None} attribute is present, an additional {@code Secure} attribute is used so cross-site cookies can only be accessed over HTTPS connections.

Accepted values are:
  • {@code Lax}
  • {@code Strict}
  • {@code None}
  • {@code Off}: Disable the generation of the SameSite cookie attribute altogether.
  • Path to a Groovy script that is able to generate the SameSite cookie attribute dynamically.
  • Fully qualified name of a class that implements {@code org.apereo.cas.web.cookie.CookieSameSitePolicy}
